translations.literal: Sons of Emperor Wu of Wei: Prince Min of Feng, Cao Ang; Prince Shang of Xiang, Cao Shuo; Prince Ai of Deng, Cao Chong; Prince of Pengcheng, Cao Ju; Prince of Yan, Cao Yu; Prince Mu of Pei, Cao Lin; Prince Gong of Zhongshan, Cao Gun; Prince Huai of Jiyang, Cao Xuan; Prince Gong of Chenliu, Cao Jun; Prince Min of Fanyang, Cao Ju (distinct from the Prince of Pengcheng); Prince of Zhao, Cao Gan; Prince Shang of Linyi, Cao Shang; Prince of Chu, Cao Biao; Prince Shang of Gang, Cao Qin; Prince Shang of Gucheng, Cao Cheng; Prince Dai of Mei, Cao Zheng; Prince Shang of Ling, Cao Jing; Duke An of Fan, Cao Jun (distinct from Prince Gong of Chenliu); Prince Shang of Guangzong, Cao Ji; Prince Ling of Dongping, Cao Hui; Prince of Leling, Cao Mao. Sons of Emperor Wen of Wei: Prince Ai of Zan, Cao Xie; Prince Dao of Beihai, Cao Rui; Prince Huai of Dongwuyang, Cao Jian; Prince Ding of Donghai, Cao Lin (distinct from Prince Mu of Pei); Prince Ai of Yuancheng, Cao Li; Prince Huai of Handan, Cao Yong; Prince Dao of Qinghe, Cao Gong; Prince Ai of Guangping, Cao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Emperor Wu of Wei: Cao Ang, posthumously Prince Min of Feng; Cao Shuo, posthumously Prince Shang of Xiang; Cao Chong, posthumously Prince Ai of Deng; Cao Ju, Prince of Pengcheng; Cao Yu, Prince of Yan; Cao Lin, posthumously Prince Mu of Pei; Cao Gun, posthumously Prince Gong of Zhongshan; Cao Xuan, posthumously Prince Huai of Jiyang; Cao Jun, posthumously Prince Gong of Chenliu; the other Cao Ju, posthumously Prince Min of Fanyang; Cao Gan, Prince of Zhao; Cao Shang, posthumously Prince Shang of Linyi; Cao Biao, Prince of Chu; Cao Qin, posthumously Prince Shang of Gang; Cao Cheng, posthumously Prince Shang of Gucheng; Cao Zheng, posthumously Prince Dai of Mei; Cao Jing, posthumously Prince Shang of Ling; Cao Jun, Duke An of Fan (not the Prince of Chenliu); Cao Ji, posthumously Prince Shang of Guangzong; Cao Hui, posthumously Prince Ling of Dongping; Cao Mao, Prince of Leling. The sons of Emperor Wen of Wei: Cao Xie, posthumously Prince Ai of Zan; Cao Rui, posthumously Prince Dao of Beihai; Cao Jian, posthumously Prince Huai of Dongwuyang; Cao Lin, posthumously Prince Ding of Donghai (not the Prince of Pei); Cao Li, posthumously Prince Ai of Yuancheng; Cao Yong, posthumously Prince Huai of Handan; Cao Gong, posthumously Prince Dao of Qinghe; Cao Yan, posthumously Prince Ai of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝诸子

translations.literal: Sons of Emperor Wu of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Emperor Wu of Wei.

sentences.zh: 武皇帝二十五男：卞皇后生文皇帝、任城威王彰、陈思王植、萧怀王熊；

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor had twenty-five sons: Empress Dowager Bian bore Emperor Wen, Prince Wei of Rencheng Cao Zhang, Prince Si of Chen Cao Zhi, and Prince Huai of Xiao Cao Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: The Martial Emperor fathered twenty-five sons. Empress Dowager Bian gave birth to Emperor Wen, Cao Zhang (Prince Wei of Rencheng), Cao Zhi (Prince Si of Chen), and Cao Xiong (Prince Huai of Xiao).

sentences.zh: 刘夫人生丰愍王昂、相殇王铄；

translations.literal: Lady Liu bore Prince Min of Feng Cao Ang and Prince Shang of Xiang Cao Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu bore Cao Ang, later honored as Prince Min of Feng, and Cao Shuo, later honored as Prince Shang of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 环夫人生邓哀王冲、彭城王据、燕王宇；

translations.literal: Lady Huan bore Prince Ai of Deng Cao Chong, the Prince of Pengcheng Cao Ju, and the Prince of Yan Cao Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Huan bore Cao Chong (Prince Ai of Deng), Cao Ju (Prince of Pengcheng), and Cao Yu (Prince of Yan).

sentences.zh: 杜夫人生沛穆王林、中山恭王衮；

translations.literal: Lady Du bore Prince Mu of Pei Cao Lin and Prince Gong of Zhongshan Cao Gun.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Du bore Cao Lin, posthumously Prince Mu of Pei, and Cao Gun, posthumously Prince Gong of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 秦夫人生济阳怀王玹、陈留恭王峻；

translations.literal: Lady Qin bore Prince Huai of Jiyang Cao Xuan and Prince Gong of Chenliu Cao Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Qin bore Cao Xuan (Prince Huai of Jiyang) and Cao Jun (Prince Gong of Chenliu).

sentences.zh: 尹夫人生范阳闵王矩；

translations.literal: Lady Yin bore Prince Min of Fanyang Cao Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yin bore Cao Ju, later titled Prince Min of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 王昭仪生赵王幹；

translations.literal: Lady Wang the honored consort bore the Prince of Zhao Cao Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Honored consort Lady Wang bore the Prince of Zhao, Cao Gan.

sentences.zh: 孙姬生临邑殇公子上、楚王彪、刚殇公子勤；

translations.literal: Lady Sun bore Prince Shang of Linyi Cao Shang, the Prince of Chu Cao Biao, and Prince Shang of Gang Cao Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Sun bore Cao Shang (Prince Shang of Linyi), Cao Biao (Prince of Chu), and Cao Qin (Prince Shang of Gang).

sentences.zh: 李姬生谷城殇公子乘、郿戴公子整、灵殇公子京；

translations.literal: Lady Li bore Prince Shang of Gucheng Cao Cheng, Prince Dai of Mei Cao Zheng, and Prince Shang of Ling Cao Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li bore Cao Cheng (Prince Shang of Gucheng), Cao Zheng (Prince Dai of Mei), and Cao Jing (Prince Shang of Ling).

sentences.zh: 周姬生樊安公均；

translations.literal: Lady Zhou bore Duke An of Fan Cao Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhou bore Cao Jun, enfeoffed as Duke An of Fan.

sentences.zh: 刘姬生广宗殇公子棘；

translations.literal: Lady Liu bore Prince Shang of Guangzong Cao Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu bore Cao Ji, posthumously Prince Shang of Guangzong.

sentences.zh: 宋姬生东平灵王徽；

translations.literal: Lady Song bore Prince Ling of Dongping Cao Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Song bore Cao Hui, posthumously Prince Ling of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 赵姬生乐陵王茂。

translations.literal: Lady Zhao bore the Prince of Leling Cao Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhao bore Cao Mao, Prince of Leling.

sentences.zh: 丰愍王曹昂

translations.literal: Prince Min of Feng, Cao Ang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ang, posthumously Prince Min of Feng.

sentences.zh: 丰愍王昂字子脩。

translations.literal: Prince Min of Feng Ang, style Zixiu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ang of Feng, styled Zixiu, bore the posthumous dignity Prince Min.

sentences.zh: 弱冠举孝廉。

translations.literal: At the weak-crown age he was recommended as filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he was recommended as filial and incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 随太祖南征，为张绣所害。

translations.literal: He accompanied the Grand Progenitor on a southern campaign and was killed by Zhang Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Cao Cao on the southern campaign and died at the hands of Zhang Xiu.

sentences.zh: 无子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir.

sentences.zh: 黄初二年追封，谥曰丰悼公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangchu he was posthumously enfeoffed, with posthumous title Prince Dao of Feng.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 2 he received a posthumous fief as Prince Dao of Feng.

sentences.zh: 三年，以樊安公均子琬奉昂后，封中都公。

translations.literal: In the third year, the son of Duke An of Fan Jun, Wan, was appointed to continue Ang's line; he was enfeoffed as duke of Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Cao Wan, son of Duke An of Fan Cao Jun, was designated Ang's heir and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 其年徙封长子公。

translations.literal: That year he was moved to a fief as duke of Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: The same year his fief was transferred and he became Duke of Changzi.

sentences.zh: 五年，追加昂号曰丰悼王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Ang's title was additionally advanced to Prince Dao of Feng.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 5 Ang's posthumous rank was raised to Prince Dao of Feng.

sentences.zh: 太和三年改昂谥曰愍王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe Ang's posthumous title was changed to Prince Min.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 3 his posthumous title was changed to Prince Min.

sentences.zh: 嘉平六年，以琬袭昂爵为丰王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaping, Wan inherited Ang's rank and became Prince of Feng.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaping 6 Cao Wan succeeded to Ang's princely rank as Prince of Feng.

sentences.zh: 正元、景元中，累增邑，并前二千七百户。

translations.literal: In the Zhengyuan and Jingyuan periods his fief was repeatedly increased, totaling 2,700 households with the earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhengyuan and Jingyuan reigns his appanage was enlarged several times until, with prior holdings, it came to 2,700 households.

sentences.zh: 琬薨，谥曰恭王。

translations.literal: Wan died; his posthumous title was Prince Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Wan died he received the posthumous name Prince Gong.

sentences.zh: 子廉嗣。

translations.literal: His son Lian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao Lian inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 相殇王曹铄

translations.literal: Prince Shang of Xiang, Cao Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuo, posthumously Prince Shang of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 相殇王铄，早薨，太和三年追封谥。

translations.literal: Prince Shang of Xiang Shuo died young; in Taihe 3 he was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuo died in childhood; in Taihe 3 he was posthumously enfeoffed and titled.

sentences.zh: 青龙元年，子愍王潜嗣，其年薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qinglong, Prince Min Qian succeeded; that year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Qinglong 1 Cao Qian, posthumously Prince Min, succeeded but died the same year.

sentences.zh: 二年，子怀王偃嗣，邑二千五百户，四年薨。

translations.literal: In the second year, Prince Huai Yan succeeded, with a fief of 2,500 households; in the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Qinglong 2 Cao Yan, posthumously Prince Huai, inherited with 2,500 households; he died in Qinglong 4.

sentences.zh: 无子，国除。

translations.literal: He had no son; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He had no heir, and the principality was abolished.

sentences.zh: 正元二年，以乐陵王茂子阳都乡公竦继铄后。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengyuan, Song, village duke of Yangdu from Prince Mao of Leling, was appointed to continue Shuo's line.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengyuan 2 Cao Song, village duke of Yangdu and son of Prince Mao of Leling, was designated heir to Shuo's line.

sentences.zh: 邓哀王曹冲

translations.literal: Prince Ai of Deng, Cao Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Chong, posthumously Prince Ai of Deng.

sentences.zh: 彭城王曹据

translations.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng, Cao Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ju, Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 燕王曹宇

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan, Cao Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yu, Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 沛穆王曹林

translations.literal: Prince Mu of Pei, Cao Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Lin, posthumously Prince Mu of Pei.

sentences.zh: 沛穆王林，建安十六年封饶阳侯。

translations.literal: Prince Mu of Pei Lin, in the sixteenth year of Jian'an, was enfeoffed marquis of Raoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 16 Cao Lin was enfeoffed as Marquis of Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，徙封谯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was moved to a fief at Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 22 his fief was moved to Qiao.

sentences.zh: 黄初二年，进爵为公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangchu his rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 2 he was promoted from marquis to duke.

sentences.zh: 三年，为谯王。

translations.literal: In the third year he became Prince of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 3 he was made Prince of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 五年，改封谯县。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his fief was changed to Qiao county.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 5 his enfeoffment was redesignated at Qiao county.

sentences.zh: 七年，徙封鄄城。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was moved to a fief at Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 7 his fief was transferred to Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 太和六年，改封沛。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe his fief was changed to Pei.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 6 he was reassigned to Pei.

sentences.zh: 景初、正元、景元中，累增邑，并前四千七百户。

translations.literal: In the Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan periods his fief was repeatedly increased, totaling 4,700 households with the earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan his appanage was enlarged repeatedly until it reached 4,700 households in all.

sentences.zh: 林薨，子纬嗣。

translations.literal: Lin died; his son Wei succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Lin died his son Cao Wei inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 〈案嵇氏谱：嵇康妻，林子之女也。〉

translations.literal: 〈According to the Ji lineage: the wife of Ji Kang was a daughter of Lin.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Ji family genealogy records that Ji Kang's wife was a daughter of Cao Lin.〉

sentences.zh: 中山恭王曹衮

translations.literal: Prince Gong of Zhongshan, Cao Gun.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Gun, posthumously Prince Gong of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 中山恭王衮，建安二十一年封平乡侯。

translations.literal: Prince Gong of Zhongshan Gun, in the twenty-first year of Jian'an, was enfeoffed marquis of Pingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 21 Cao Gun was first enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 少好学，年十餘岁能属文。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning; at age ten-odd he could compose essays.
translations.idiomatic: He loved scholarship from boyhood and, before he was twenty, could already write polished essays.

sentences.zh: 每读书，文学左右常恐以精力为病，数谏止之，然性所乐，不能废也。

translations.literal: Whenever he read, his literary attendants on left and right often feared illness from exertion of spirit and strength, and repeatedly remonstrated and stopped him, yet what his nature delighted in he could not abandon.
translations.idiomatic: When he immersed himself in books, his literary tutors and guards worried that he would ruin his health and often urged him to stop, but the habit was in his nature and he could not give it up.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，徙封东乡侯，其年又改封赞侯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was moved to marquis of Dongxiang; that year it was again changed to marquis of Zan.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 22 he was transferred to Marquis of Dongxiang, then in the same year redesignated Marquis of Zan.

sentences.zh: 黄初二年，进爵为公，官属皆贺，衮曰：“夫生深宫之中，不知稼穑之艰难，多骄逸之失。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangchu his rank was advanced to duke; his officials all congratulated him, and Gun said, "Born deep within the palace, one does not know the hardships of sowing and reaping; there is much fault in pride and dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 2 he was raised to duke. When his household officers offered congratulations, Gun said, "A man raised deep in the inner palaces never learns how hard it is to fill the granary; that ignorance breeds arrogance and excess.

sentences.zh: 诸贤既庆其休，宜辅其阙。

translations.literal: You worthies have rejoiced in my good fortune; you ought to remedy my shortcomings."
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen rejoice in my good name; you should be helping me mend my faults."

sentences.zh: ”每兄弟游娱，衮独覃思经典。

translations.literal: Whenever the brothers roamed in pleasure, Gun alone pondered deeply the classics.
translations.idiomatic: While his brothers went off in sport, he alone stayed with the classics, lost in thought.

sentences.zh: 文学防辅相与言曰：“受诏察公举错，有过当奏，及有善，亦宜以闻，不可匿其美也。

translations.literal: The literary defenders and tutors said to one another, "We received orders to observe the duke's conduct; if there are faults we should memorialize, and if there are good points we should also report them—we may not hide his excellence."
translations.idiomatic: His literary tutors and minders said among themselves, "We are charged to watch the duke's conduct: faults must go up in memorials, but virtues must be reported too—we are not to conceal what is praiseworthy."

sentences.zh: ”遂共表称陈衮美。

translations.literal: Thereupon together they submitted a memorial praising Gun's excellence.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore jointly memorialized the throne, praising Gun's virtues.

sentences.zh: 衮闻之，大惊惧，责让文学曰：“脩身自守，常人之行耳，而诸君乃以上闻，是適所以增其负累也。

translations.literal: When Gun heard of it he was greatly alarmed and afraid, and rebuked the literary men, saying, "Cultivating the person and guarding oneself is the conduct of ordinary men, yet you gentlemen have reported it upward—this is precisely what increases my burden.
translations.idiomatic: Gun was terrified when he heard of it and rebuked them: "Self-discipline is what any decent man does, yet you have laid it before the throne; that only heaps new burdens on me.

sentences.zh: 且如有善，何患不闻，而遽共如是，是非益我者。

translations.literal: Moreover if there were good points, what worry that they would not be heard, yet hastily you act together thus—this is not what benefits me."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, if I had real merit, would it not become known in time? To rush a joint memorial like this does me no good at all."

sentences.zh: ”其戒慎如此。

translations.literal: His caution and fearfulness were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the anxious care with which he guarded himself.

sentences.zh: 三年，为北海王。

translations.literal: In the third year he became Prince of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 3 he was made Prince of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 其年，黄龙见鄴西漳水，衮上书赞颂。

translations.literal: That year a yellow dragon appeared in the Zhang River west of Ye; Gun submitted a memorial in praise.
translations.idiomatic: That year a yellow dragon was seen in the Zhang west of Ye, and Gun sent up a hymn of praise.

sentences.zh: 诏赐黄金十斤，诏曰：“昔唐叔归禾，东平献颂，斯皆骨肉赞美，以彰懿亲。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed ten catties of gold, and the edict said, "In olden days Tang Shu returned grain ears and the Prince of Dongping presented a hymn—such were bone-and-flesh kin praising one another to display close kinship.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent ten catties of gold with an edict: "Long ago Tang Shu offered the doubled ears of grain, and the Prince of Dongping offered his ode—kinfolk honoring one another to show the grace of the royal house.

sentences.zh: 王研精坟典，耽味道真，文雅焕炳，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: The prince has studied the grave texts to the depths, indulged in the flavor of the true Way, and his refined letters shine brightly; I greatly approve."
translations.idiomatic: You have steeped yourself in the canon and savored the true Way; your literary voice is radiant, and I am well pleased."

sentences.zh: 王其克慎明德，以终令闻。

translations.literal: Prince, be able to be cautious in bright virtue, to complete your fair reputation."
translations.idiomatic: Prince, hold fast to enlightened virtue and so preserve the good name you have won."

sentences.zh: ”四年，改封赞王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year his fief was changed to Prince of Zan.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 4 he was redesignated Prince of Zan.

sentences.zh: 七年，徙封濮阳。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was moved to a fief at Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 7 his seat was moved to Puyang.

sentences.zh: 太和二年就国，尚约俭，教敕妃妾纺绩织纴，习为家人之事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe he went to his state, was still frugal and restrained, and ordered his consorts and concubines to spin and weave, practicing household tasks of a common family.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 2 he took up residence in his fief, lived plainly, and made his consorts spin and weave like any modest household.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，入朝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, winter, he entered court.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Taihe 5 he came to the capital for audience.

sentences.zh: 六年，改封中山。

translations.literal: In the sixth year his fief was changed to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 6 he was transferred to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 初，衮来朝，犯京都禁。

translations.literal: At first, when Gun came to court, he violated the capital prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on a visit to court, Gun had broken a capital ordinance.

sentences.zh: 青龙元年，有司奏衮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qinglong, the responsible officials memorialized Gun.
translations.idiomatic: In Qinglong 1 the authorities impeached him.

sentences.zh: 诏曰：“王素敬慎，邂逅至此，其以议亲之典议之。

translations.literal: The edict said, "The prince has always been reverent and cautious; meeting with this, apply the precedent for deliberating on kin."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "The prince has always been dutiful and careful; treat this slip under the rules that govern punishment of imperial kin."

sentences.zh: ”有司固执。

translations.literal: The responsible officials obstinately held to their view.
translations.idiomatic: The officials refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 诏削县二，户七百五十。

translations.literal: An edict stripped two counties, 750 households.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then removed two counties from his fief, cutting 750 households.

sentences.zh: 〈魏书载玺书曰：“制诏中山王：有司奏，王乃者来朝，犯交通京师之禁。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei shu records the text of the seal-edict: "Ordered: to the Prince of Zhongshan. The authorities report that on your recent visit to court you violated the prohibition on traffic with the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Book of Wei preserves the sealed rescript: "Let it be proclaimed to the Prince of Zhongshan: the ministers report that on your last visit you broke the rule forbidding private movement in and out of the capital zone.

sentences.zh: 朕惟亲亲之恩，用寝吏议。

translations.literal: I ponder the grace of cherishing kin and therefore set aside the clerks' deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Out of love for my kinsman I would have set their recommendation aside.

sentences.zh: 然法者，所与天下共也，不可得废。

translations.literal: Yet the law is what is shared with all under Heaven; it cannot be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: But law is the common bond of the realm; it cannot simply be waived.

sentences.zh: 今削王县二，户七百五十。

translations.literal: Now strip the prince of two counties, 750 households.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore remove two counties from your fief, 750 households in all.

sentences.zh: 夫克己复礼，圣人称仁，朝过夕改，君子与之。

translations.literal: To restrain oneself and return to ritual the sage called benevolence; morning fault, evening reform—the gentleman approves it.
translations.idiomatic: The sages called self-mastery and return to ritual the root of humanity; to mend a fault the same day wins a gentleman's praise.

sentences.zh: 王其戒诸，无贰咎悔也。

translations.literal: Prince, guard yourself in these things; do not again incur blame and regret."
translations.idiomatic: Prince, take this as your warning and do not invite fresh blame or remorse."

translations.literal: The text gives a closing quotation mark and angle bracket, marking the end of the Wei shu quotation.
translations.idiomatic: The quoted edict ends here and the Wei shu excerpt closes.

sentences.zh: 衮忧惧，戒敕官属愈谨。

translations.literal: Gun was worried and afraid, and warned and ordered his subordinates to be still more careful.
translations.idiomatic: Gun lived in fear after that and lectured his officers to be doubly scrupulous.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其意，二年，复所削县。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his intent; in the second year he restored the stripped counties.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his contrition, and in the second year returned the two counties.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，衮得疾病，诏遣太医视疾，殿中、虎贲赍手诏、赐珍膳相属，又遣太妃、沛王林并就省疾。

translations.literal: In the third year, autumn, Gun fell ill; an edict sent the imperial physicians to treat the illness, palace attendants and tiger guards brought autograph edicts in succession and bestowed fine viands, and also sent the grand consort and Prince Lin of Pei together to inquire after the illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Qinglong 3 he fell gravely ill. The throne sent the court physicians, then couriers from the palace guard bearing autograph orders and rare foods, and finally the grand consort and Prince Lin of Pei to his bedside.

sentences.zh: 衮疾困，敕令官属曰：“吾寡德忝宠，大命将尽。

translations.literal: Gun's illness was severe; he ordered his subordinates, saying, "My scant virtue shamefully enjoys favor; the great mandate is about to end.
translations.idiomatic: As his strength failed he told his officers, "My slight virtue has been overfavored; my allotted span is almost spent.

sentences.zh: 吾既好俭，而圣朝著终诰之制，为天下法。

translations.literal: I have both loved frugality, and the sage court has established regulations for the end, as a model for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: I have always loved simplicity, and the sage court's rules for burial are the model for the world.

sentences.zh: 吾气绝之日，自殡及葬，务奉诏书。

translations.literal: On the day my breath ends, from encoffining to burial, be sure to obey the edict letters.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment I die through encoffining and interment, you must follow the edicts to the letter.

sentences.zh: 昔卫大夫蘧瑗葬濮阳，吾望其墓，常想其遗风，原讬贤灵以弊发齿，营吾兆域，必往从之。

translations.literal: In olden days the Wei grandee Qu Yuan was buried at Puyang; I have gazed on his tomb and often pondered his surviving style; I desire to entrust my decayed hair and teeth to his worthy spirit, so that in laying out my burial ground I must go and follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Qu Yuan of Wei was buried at Puyang; whenever I passed his mound I thought of his example, and I wish to lay these failing bones beside his dust so my tomb may stand near his.

sentences.zh: 礼：男子不卒妇人之手。

translations.literal: Ritual: a man does not expire in a woman's hands.
translations.idiomatic: The rites say a man must not draw his last breath in a woman's arms.

sentences.zh: 亟以时成东堂。

translations.literal: Hasten to complete in due time the east hall.
translations.idiomatic: Finish the east hall quickly, within the proper time.

sentences.zh: ”堂成，名之曰遂志之堂，舆疾往居之。

translations.literal: When the hall was completed he named it the Hall of Fulfilling My Resolve, and in a litter, ill, went to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: When it was done he named it the Hall Where My Purpose Is Fulfilled and had himself carried there, sick as he was.

sentences.zh: 又令世子曰：“汝幼少，未闻义方，早为人君，但知乐，不知苦；

translations.literal: He also ordered the heir apparent, saying, "You are young and small, have not heard the right way, early became ruler of men, know only pleasure, do not know hardship;
translations.idiomatic: He also instructed his heir: "You are still a child, untaught in duty, yet you will soon be a lord of men; you know joy but not hardship;

sentences.zh: 不知苦，必将以骄奢为失也。

translations.literal: not knowing hardship, you will surely take arrogance and luxury as fault."
translations.idiomatic: and a man who does not know hardship will lose himself in pride and waste."

sentences.zh: 接大臣，务以礼。

translations.literal: Receive great ministers, be sure to use ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Treat great ministers always with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 虽非大臣，老者犹宜答拜。

translations.literal: Even if not great ministers, old men still ought to be answered with bowing.
translations.idiomatic: Even toward men of lesser rank, if they are old, return their courtesy with a bow.

sentences.zh: 事兄以敬，恤弟以慈；

translations.literal: Serve the elder brother with respect, pity the younger brothers with kindness;
translations.idiomatic: Honor your elder brother; be gentle with your younger brothers;

sentences.zh: 兄弟有不良之行，当造膝谏之。

translations.literal: if brothers have ungood conduct, you ought to go to the knee and remonstrate them.
translations.idiomatic: and if a brother goes wrong, take him aside and counsel him until he listens.

sentences.zh: 谏之不从，流涕喻之；

translations.literal: If remonstrating they do not obey, weep tears and instruct them;
translations.idiomatic: If they will not heed your counsel, plead with them through tears;

sentences.zh: 喻之不改，乃白其母。

translations.literal: If instructing them they do not reform, then report to their mother.
translations.idiomatic: and if gentle words fail to change them, take the matter to their mother.

sentences.zh: 若犹不改，当以奏闻，并辞国土。

translations.literal: If still they do not reform, you ought to memorialize and inform, and together resign the territory of the state.
translations.idiomatic: If they still refuse to mend their ways, memorialize the throne and be prepared to surrender your fief along with the report.

sentences.zh: 与其守宠罹祸，不若贫贱全身也。

translations.literal: Compared with guarding favor and encountering disaster, it is not like being lowly and poor and preserving the whole body.
translations.idiomatic: Better to live in poverty with your integrity intact than to cling to favor and court ruin.

sentences.zh: 此亦谓大罪恶耳，其微过细故，当掩覆之。

translations.literal: This also speaks of great wickedness and evil; as for minute faults and trivial matters, you ought to cover and conceal them.
translations.idiomatic: That applies to grave vice; for petty slips and trifling offenses, cover them in silence.

sentences.zh: 嗟尔小子，慎脩乃身，奉圣朝以忠贞，事太妃以孝敬。

translations.literal: Alas you young child, carefully cultivate your person, serve the sage court with loyalty and steadfastness, serve the grand consort with filial respect.
translations.idiomatic: My child, cherish your conduct: serve the dynasty with loyal devotion and honor the grand dowager with true filial piety.

sentences.zh: 闺闱之内，奉令於太妃；

translations.literal: Within the inner chambers, obey orders from the grand consort;
translations.idiomatic: Within the women's quarters, obey the grand dowager in all things;

sentences.zh: 阃阈之外，受教於沛王。

translations.literal: Outside the inner threshold, receive instruction from the Prince of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: beyond those doors take your guidance from the Prince of Pei.

sentences.zh: 无怠乃心，以慰予灵。

translations.literal: Do not slacken your heart, thereby to comfort my spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let your heart grow idle; let that be your comfort to my spirit.

sentences.zh: ”其年薨。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died later that same year.

sentences.zh: 诏沛王林留讫葬，使大鸿胪持节典护丧事，宗正吊祭，赠赗甚厚。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince Lin of Pei to remain until burial was finished, sent the grand herald with staff of authority to oversee the funeral, the director of the imperial clan to offer condolences and sacrifices, and gifts for the dead were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Prince Lin of Pei to stay through the burial, placed the chief protocol officer in charge of the rites with imperial credentials, had the director of the imperial clan conduct the mourning sacrifices, and sent exceptionally rich grave goods.

sentences.zh: 凡所著文章二万餘言，才不及陈思王而好与之侔。

translations.literal: In all, the writings he composed were more than twenty thousand words; his talent did not reach the Prince Si of Chen, yet he loved to rival him.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings run to more than twenty thousand characters—less brilliant than Cao Zhi, the Prince of Chen, though he measured himself against him.

sentences.zh: 子孚嗣。

translations.literal: His son Fu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao Fu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 景初、正元、景元中，累增邑，并前三千四百户。

translations.literal: In the Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan periods his fief was repeatedly increased, totaling 3,400 households with the earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan his appanage was enlarged several times until, with earlier holdings, it stood at 3,400 households.

sentences.zh: 济阳怀王曹玹

translations.literal: Prince Huai of Jiyang, Cao Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xuan, posthumously Prince Huai of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 济阳怀王玹，建安十六年封西乡侯。

translations.literal: Prince Huai of Jiyang Xuan, in the sixteenth year of Jian'an, was enfeoffed marquis of Xixiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 16 Cao Xuan was first made Marquis of Xixiang.

sentences.zh: 早薨，无子。

translations.literal: He died young; he had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He died in childhood without leaving an heir.

sentences.zh: 二十年，以沛王林子赞袭玹爵邑，早薨，无子。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Zan, son of the Prince of Pei Lin, inherited Xuan's rank and fief, died young, had no son.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 20 Cao Zan, son of Prince Lin of Pei, was appointed to continue Xuan's line but died young and childless.

sentences.zh: 文帝复以赞弟壹绍玹后。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen again used Zan's younger brother Yi to continue Xuan's line.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen then designated Zan's younger brother Cao Yi as heir to Xuan.

sentences.zh: 黄初二年，改封济阳侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangchu his fief was changed to marquis of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 2 he was transferred to the Marquisate of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 四年，进爵为公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year his rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 4 he was promoted to duke.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，追进玹爵，谥曰怀公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe Xuan's rank was posthumously advanced, posthumous title Prince Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 4 Xuan's posthumous rank was raised and he was titled Prince Huai.

sentences.zh: 六年，又进号曰怀王，追谥赞曰西乡哀侯。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, again his title was advanced to Prince Huai, and Zan was posthumously titled marquis Ai of Xixiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 6 he was further honored as Prince Huai of Jiyang, while Zan received the posthumous title Marquis Ai of Xixiang.

sentences.zh: 壹薨，谥曰悼公。

translations.literal: Yi died; posthumous title Prince Dao.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Yi died he was posthumously titled Prince Dao.

sentences.zh: 子恆嗣。

translations.literal: His son Heng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao Heng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 景初、正元、景元中，累增邑，并前千九百户。

translations.literal: In the Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan periods his fief was repeatedly increased, totaling 1,900 households with the earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan his fief grew until it reached 1,900 households in all.

sentences.zh: 陈留恭王曹峻

translations.literal: Prince Gong of Chenliu, Cao Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jun, posthumously Prince Gong of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 陈留恭王峻字子安，建安二十一年封郿侯。

translations.literal: Prince Gong of Chenliu Jun, style Zian, in the twenty-first year of Jian'an was enfeoffed marquis of Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jun, styled Zian, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Mei in Jian'an 21.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，徙封襄邑。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was moved to a fief at Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 22 his seat was moved to Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 黄初二年，进爵为公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangchu his rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 2 he was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 三年，为陈留王。

translations.literal: In the third year he became Prince of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 3 he became Prince of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 五年，改封襄邑县。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his fief was changed to Xiangyi county.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 5 his enfeoffment was fixed at Xiangyi county.

sentences.zh: 太和六年，又封陈留。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe he was again enfeoffed at Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 6 he was again assigned to Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 甘露四年薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Ganlu he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Ganlu 4.

sentences.zh: 子澳嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao Ao inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 景初、正元、景元中，累增邑，并前四千七百户。

translations.literal: In the Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan periods his fief was repeatedly increased, totaling 4,700 households with the earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan his appanage was enlarged until it reached 4,700 households with prior grants.

sentences.zh: 范阳闵王曹矩

translations.literal: Prince Min of Fanyang, Cao Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ju of Fanyang, posthumously Prince Min.

sentences.zh: 范阳闵王矩，早薨，无子。

translations.literal: Prince Min of Fanyang Ju died young; he had no son.
translations.idiomatic: This Cao Ju died in infancy without an heir.

sentences.zh: 建安二十二年，以樊安公均子敏奉矩后，封临晋侯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Jian'an, Min, son of Duke An of Fan Jun, was appointed to continue Ju's line, enfeoffed marquis of Linjin.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 22 Cao Min, son of Duke An of Fan, was named heir to Ju's line and enfeoffed as Marquis of Linjin.

sentences.zh: 黄初三年追封谥矩为范阳闵公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangchu posthumous enfeoffment and posthumous title were conferred on Ju as Prince Min of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 3 Ju was posthumously honored as Prince Min of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 五年，改封敏范阳王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Min was changed to enfeoffment as Prince of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 5 Cao Min was made Prince of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 七年，徙封句阳，太和六年，追进矩号曰范阳闵王，改封敏琅邪王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was moved to a fief at Gouyang; in the sixth year of Taihe Ju's title was posthumously advanced to Prince Min of Fanyang, and Min was changed to enfeoffment as Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 7 his fief moved to Gouyang; in Taihe 6 Ju's posthumous rank was raised to Prince Min of Fanyang, and Cao Min was transferred to the princedom of Langye.

sentences.zh: 景初、正元、景元中，累增邑，并前三千四百户。

translations.literal: In the Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan periods his fief was repeatedly increased, totaling 3,400 households with the earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: Across Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan his holdings rose to 3,400 households including earlier grants.

sentences.zh: 敏薨，谥曰原王。

translations.literal: Min died; posthumous title Prince Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Min died he received the posthumous name Prince Yuan.

sentences.zh: 子焜嗣。

translations.literal: His son Kun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao Kun inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 赵王曹幹

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhao, Cao Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Gan, Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 赵王幹，建安二十年封高平亭侯。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhao Gan, in the twentieth year of Jian'an, was enfeoffed marquis of Gaoping village.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 20 Cao Gan was made village marquis of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，徙封赖亭侯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was moved to marquis of Lai village.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 22 he was transferred to village marquis of Lai.

sentences.zh: 其年改封弘农侯。

translations.literal: That year it was changed to marquis of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: The same year he was redesignated Marquis of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 黄初二年，进爵，徙封燕公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangchu his rank was advanced and he was moved to enfeoffment as duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 2 he was promoted and given the ducal fief of Yan.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：幹一名良。

translations.literal: 〈The Wei lue says: Gan had another name Liang.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wei lue records that Cao Gan was also called Liang.

sentences.zh: 良本陈妾子，良生而陈氏死，太祖令王夫人养之。

translations.literal: Liang was originally a son of Lady Chen the concubine; when Liang was born Lady Chen died, and the Grand Progenitor ordered Lady Wang to raise him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was born to Lady Chen; she died at his birth, and Cao Cao placed the boy in Lady Wang's care.

sentences.zh: 良年五岁而太祖疾困，遗令语太子曰：“此兒三岁亡母，五岁失父，以累汝也。

translations.literal: When Liang was five years old the Grand Progenitor was critically ill; dying instructions told the heir apparent: "This child at three lost his mother, at five loses his father, thereby burdening you.
translations.idiomatic: At five Liang stood by Cao Cao's deathbed; the dying patriarch told the heir, "He lost his mother at three and will lose his father at five—you must bear the burden for him.

sentences.zh: ”太子由是亲待，隆於诸弟。

translations.literal: The heir apparent therefore treated him intimately, more than the various younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince therefore favored him above his other younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 良年小，常呼文帝为阿翁，帝谓良曰：“我，汝兄耳。

translations.literal: Liang being young, often called Emperor Wen "A-weng"; Emperor Wen told Liang: "I am your elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liang was still a child he often called Emperor Wen "Daddy"; Wen answered gently, "I am your elder brother, not your father.

sentences.zh: ”文帝又愍其如是，每为流涕。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen also pitied him being thus, and for it often wept.
translations.idiomatic: The sight moved Emperor Wen so deeply that he often wept for him.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：此传以母贵贱为次，不计兄弟之年，故楚王彪年虽大，传在幹后。

translations.literal: Your subject Song Zhi notes: this biography orders by the noble or base rank of mothers, not calculating the years of brothers, therefore though the Prince of Chu Biao is greater in years, the biography is after Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi remarks: this chapter ranks sons by their mothers' status, not by age, which is why Cao Biao, though older, appears after Cao Gan.

sentences.zh: 寻《朱建平传》，知彪大幹二十岁。〉

translations.literal: Seeking in the "Biography of Zhu Jianping," one knows Biao was twenty years greater than Gan.〉
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jianping's biography shows that Biao was a full twenty years older than Gan.〉

sentences.zh: 三年，为河间王。

translations.literal: In the third year he became Prince of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 3 he became Prince of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 五年，改封乐城县。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his fief was changed to Lecheng county.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 5 his seat was moved to Lecheng county.

sentences.zh: 七年，徙封钜鹿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was moved to a fief at Julu.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 7 he was transferred to Julu.

sentences.zh: 太和六年，改封赵王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe his fief was changed to Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 6 he was made Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 幹母有宠於太祖。

translations.literal: Gan's mother had favor with the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Gan's mother had been a favorite of Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 及文帝为嗣，幹母有力。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen became heir, Gan's mother had power.
translations.idiomatic: She also wielded influence when Emperor Wen was named heir.

sentences.zh: 文帝临崩，有遗诏，是以明帝常加恩意。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen faced death there was a dying edict; therefore Emperor Ming often added grace and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen left a deathbed testament on her account, so Emperor Ming treated Gan with special kindness.

sentences.zh: 青龙二年，私通宾客，为有司所奏，赐幹玺书诫诲之，曰：

translations.literal: In the second year of Qinglong he privately associated with guests and retainers, was memorialized by the responsible officials, and was given a seal-edict of Gan warning and instructing him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In Qinglong 2 he was impeached for maintaining improper ties with guests and clients; the throne answered with a sealed rescript of admonition that read:

sentences.zh: 景初、正元、景元中，累增邑，并前五千户。

translations.literal: In the Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan periods his fief was repeatedly increased, totaling 5,000 households with the earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan his fief was enlarged until it reached 5,000 households in all.

sentences.zh: 临邑殇公子曹上

translations.literal: Prince Shang of Linyi, Cao Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shang, posthumously Prince Shang of Linyi.

sentences.zh: 临邑殇公子上，早薨。

translations.literal: Prince Shang of Linyi Shang died young.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shang died in childhood.

sentences.zh: 太和五年，追封谥。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe posthumous enfeoffment and posthumous title were conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 5 he received a posthumous fief and title.

sentences.zh: 无后。

translations.literal: He had no successor.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir.

sentences.zh: 楚王曹彪

translations.literal: The Prince of Chu, Cao Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Biao, Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 刚殇公子曹勤

translations.literal: Prince Shang of Gang, Cao Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Qin, posthumously Prince Shang of Gang.

sentences.zh: 刚殇公子勤，早薨。

translations.literal: Prince Shang of Gang Qin died young.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Qin died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 太和五年追封谥。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe posthumous enfeoffment and posthumous title were conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 5 he was posthumously enfeoffed and titled.

sentences.zh: 无后。

translations.literal: He had no successor.
translations.idiomatic: No heir succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 谷城殇公子曹乘

translations.literal: Prince Shang of Gucheng, Cao Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cheng, posthumously Prince Shang of Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 谷城殇公子乘，早薨。

translations.literal: Prince Shang of Gucheng Cheng died young.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cheng died in childhood.

sentences.zh: 太和五年追封谥。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe posthumous enfeoffment and posthumous title were conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 5 he received posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 无后。

translations.literal: He had no successor.
translations.idiomatic: He had no posterity.

sentences.zh: 郿戴公子曹整

translations.literal: Prince Dai of Mei, Cao Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zheng, posthumously Prince Dai of Mei.

sentences.zh: 郿戴公子整，奉从叔父郎中绍后。

translations.literal: Prince Dai of Mei Zheng was appointed heir to continue the line of his father's younger cousin, Palace Gentleman Cao Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zheng was made heir to his father's cousin Cao Shao, who held the rank of palace gentleman.

sentences.zh: 建安二十二年，封郿侯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Jian'an he was enfeoffed marquis of Mei.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 22 he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Mei.

sentences.zh: 二十三年薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jian'an 23.

sentences.zh: 无子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He died without a son.

sentences.zh: 黄初二年追进爵，谥曰戴公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangchu his rank was posthumously advanced, posthumous title Prince Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 2 his rank was raised posthumously and he was titled Prince Dai.

sentences.zh: 以彭城王据子范奉整后。

translations.literal: Fan, son of the Prince of Pengcheng Ju, was appointed to continue Zheng's line.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Fan, son of Prince Ju of Pengcheng, was designated heir to Zheng.

sentences.zh: 三年，封平氏侯。

translations.literal: In the third year he was enfeoffed marquis of Pingshi.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 3 he became Marquis of Pingshi.

sentences.zh: 四年，徙封成武。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was moved to a fief at Chengwu.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 4 his fief was moved to Chengwu.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，进爵为公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe his rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 3 he was promoted to duke.

sentences.zh: 青龙三年薨。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qinglong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qinglong 3.

sentences.zh: 谥曰悼公。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Prince Dao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Prince Dao.

sentences.zh: 无后。

translations.literal: He had no successor.
translations.idiomatic: He too left no heir.

sentences.zh: 四年，诏以范弟东安乡公阐为郿公，奉整后。

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict ordered Kan, younger brother of Fan, village duke of Dong'an, to be duke of Mei, continuing Zheng's line.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year an edict named Fan's younger brother Cao Kan, village duke of Dong'an, as Duke of Mei to continue Zheng's line.

sentences.zh: 正元、景元中、累增邑，并前千八百户。

translations.literal: In the Zhengyuan and Jingyuan periods his fief was repeatedly increased, totaling 1,800 households with the earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengyuan and Jingyuan his appanage grew to 1,800 households with prior grants.

sentences.zh: 灵殇公子曹京

translations.literal: Prince Shang of Ling, Cao Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jing, posthumously Prince Shang of Ling.

sentences.zh: 灵殇公子京，早薨。

translations.literal: Prince Shang of Ling Jing died young.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jing died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 太和五年追封谥。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe posthumous enfeoffment and posthumous title were conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 5 he received posthumous enfeoffment and a posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 无后。

translations.literal: He had no successor.
translations.idiomatic: No successor was named.

sentences.zh: 樊安公曹均

translations.literal: Duke An of Fan, Cao Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jun, Duke An of Fan.

sentences.zh: 樊安公均，奉叔父蓟恭公彬后。

translations.literal: Duke An of Fan Jun was appointed to continue the line of his paternal uncle Prince Gong of Ji Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jun, Duke An of Fan, was made heir to his uncle Cao Bin, posthumously Prince Gong of Ji.

sentences.zh: 建安二十二年，封樊侯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Jian'an he was enfeoffed marquis of Fan.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 22 he received the marquisate of Fan.

sentences.zh: 二十四年薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jian'an 24.

sentences.zh: 子抗嗣。

translations.literal: His son Kang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao Kang inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 黄初二年，追进公爵，谥曰安公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangchu his rank was posthumously advanced to duke, posthumous title Duke An.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 2 he was posthumously promoted to duke with the name Duke An.

sentences.zh: 三年，徙封抗蓟公。

translations.literal: In the third year Kang was moved to enfeoffment as duke of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 3 Cao Kang was transferred to the ducal fief of Ji.

sentences.zh: 四年，徙封屯留公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was moved to enfeoffment as duke of Tunliu.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 4 his seat moved to Tunliu.

sentences.zh: 景初元年薨，谥曰定公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingchu he died, posthumous title Duke Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jingchu 1 and was posthumously titled Duke Ding.

sentences.zh: 子谌嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao Chen succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 景初、正元、景元中，累增邑，并前千九百户。

translations.literal: In the Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan periods his fief was repeatedly increased, totaling 1,900 households with the earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan his appanage grew to 1,900 households including earlier grants.

sentences.zh: 广宗殇公子曹棘

translations.literal: Prince Shang of Guangzong, Cao Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ji, posthumously Prince Shang of Guangzong.

sentences.zh: 广宗殇公子棘，早薨。

translations.literal: Prince Shang of Guangzong Ji died young.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ji died in childhood.

sentences.zh: 太和五年追封谥。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe posthumous enfeoffment and posthumous title were conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 5 he received posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 无后。

translations.literal: He had no successor.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir.

sentences.zh: 东平灵王曹徽

translations.literal: Prince Ling of Dongping, Cao Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hui, posthumously Prince Ling of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 东平灵王徽，奉叔公朗陵哀侯玉后。

translations.literal: Prince Ling of Dongping Hui was appointed to continue the line of his paternal great-uncle Langling Marquis Ai Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hui was made heir to his great-uncle Cao Yu, posthumously Marquis Ai of Langling.

sentences.zh: 建安二十二年，封历城侯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Jian'an he was enfeoffed marquis of Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 22 he became Marquis of Licheng.

sentences.zh: 黄初二年，进爵为公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangchu his rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 2 he was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 三年，为庐江王。

translations.literal: In the third year he became Prince of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 3 he was made Prince of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 四年，徙封寿张王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was moved to a fief as Prince of Shouzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 4 his princedom moved to Shouzhang.

sentences.zh: 五年，改封寿张县。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his fief was changed to Shouzhang county.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 5 his seat was fixed at Shouzhang county.

sentences.zh: 太和六年，改封东平。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe his fief was changed to Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 6 he became Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 青龙二年，徽使官属挝寿张县吏，为有司所奏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qinglong Hui ordered his subordinates to beat the clerk of Shouzhang county, and was memorialized by the responsible officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Qinglong 2 he had his officers flog a county clerk of Shouzhang and was impeached for it.

sentences.zh: 诏削县一，户五百。

translations.literal: An edict stripped one county, 500 households.
translations.idiomatic: The court removed one county from his fief, cutting five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 其年复所削县。

translations.literal: That year the stripped county was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The same year that county was given back.

sentences.zh: 正始三年薨。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengshi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhengshi 3.

sentences.zh: 子翕嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao Xi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 景初、正元、景元中，累增邑，并前三千四百户。

translations.literal: In the Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan periods his fief was repeatedly increased, totaling 3,400 households with the earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: Across Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan his holdings rose to 3,400 households in all.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：翕入晋，封廪丘公。

translations.literal: 〈Your subject Song Zhi notes: when Xi entered Jin he was enfeoffed duke of Linqiu.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Pei Songzhi remarks: after Xi submitted to the Jin dynasty he was enfeoffed as Duke of Linqiu.

sentences.zh: 魏宗室之中，名次鄄城公。

translations.literal: Among Wei imperial clansmen his place in the roster followed the Duke of Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Among Wei imperial kinsmen his name was listed after the Duke of Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 至泰始二年，翕遣世子琨奉表来朝。

translations.literal: By the second year of Taishi Xi had his heir apparent Kun present a memorial and come to court.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi 2 Xi sent his heir Cao Kun to court with a memorial of allegiance.

sentences.zh: 诏曰：“翕秉德履道，魏宗之良。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Xi holds to virtue and walks the Way; he is a good man of the Wei imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "Cao Xi keeps to virtue and the Way; he is an honorable scion of the house of Wei.

sentences.zh: 今琨远至，其假世子印绶，加骑都尉，赐服一具，钱十万，随才叙用。

translations.literal: Now Kun has come from afar; lend him the heir apparent's seal and ribbon, add cavalry commandant, bestow one set of robes, 100,000 cash, and appoint him according to his talents."
translations.idiomatic: Now that Kun has journeyed so far, invest him with the heir's seals and cords, add the title of cavalry commandant, give him a full set of court dress, a hundred thousand cash, and employ him as his abilities warrant."

sentences.zh: ”翕撰解寒食散方，与皇甫谧所撰并行於世。〉

translations.literal: Xi composed formulas explaining cold-food powder, and they circulated in the world together with what Huangfu Mi composed.〉
translations.idiomatic: Xi also wrote a treatise on formulas for cold-food dispersal drugs that circulated alongside the work of Huangfu Mi.〉

sentences.zh: 乐陵王曹茂

translations.literal: The Prince of Leling, Cao Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Mao, Prince of Leling.

sentences.zh: 乐陵王茂，建安二十二年封万岁亭侯。

translations.literal: The Prince of Leling Mao, in the twenty-second year of Jian'an, was enfeoffed marquis of Wansui village.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 22 Cao Mao was made village marquis of Wansui.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，改封平舆侯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year his fief was changed to marquis of Pingyu.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 23 he was transferred to Marquis of Pingyu.

sentences.zh: 黄初三年，进爵，徙封乘氏公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangchu his rank was advanced and he was moved to enfeoffment as duke of Chengshi.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 3 he was promoted and given the ducal fief of Chengshi.

sentences.zh: 七年，徙封中丘。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was moved to a fief at Zhongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 7 his seat moved to Zhongqiu.

sentences.zh: 茂性泬佷，少无宠於太祖。

translations.literal: Mao by nature was narrow and stubborn, and in youth had no favor with the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Mao was surly and obstinate by nature and had never won Cao Cao's affection.

sentences.zh: 及文帝世，又独不王。

translations.literal: Coming to Emperor Wen's reign, again alone he was not made prince.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen he alone among the brothers was never raised to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 太和元年，徙封聊城公，其年为王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe he was moved to enfeoffment as duke of Liaocheng; that year he became king.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 1 he was made Duke of Liaocheng and the same year promoted to king.

sentences.zh: 诏曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: The edict read:

sentences.zh: 昔象之为虐至甚，而大舜犹侯之有庳。

translations.literal: In olden days Xiang's cruelty was extreme, yet great Shun still enfeoffed him at Youbi.
translations.idiomatic: Even when Xiang was at his cruel worst, Shun still gave him a fief at Youbi.

sentences.zh: 近汉氏淮南、阜陵，皆为乱臣逆子，而犹或及身而复国，或至子而锡土。

translations.literal: In recent Han times the Princes of Huainan and Fuling were all rebellious ministers and unfilial sons, yet some regained their states in their own lifetimes, or down to sons received land.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, the kings of Huainan and Fuling were traitors and unfilial sons, yet some won back their kingdoms in their own day, or saw their sons enfeoffed again.

sentences.zh: 有虞建之於上古，汉文、明、章行之乎前代，斯皆敦叙亲亲之厚义也。

translations.literal: You Yu established this in high antiquity; Han Wen, Ming, and Zhang practiced it in former ages—these all are thick meanings of generously ordering dear kin.
translations.idiomatic: The model runs back to high antiquity under Shun, and Han Wendi, Mingdi, and Zhangdi upheld it—the deep duty of cherishing one's own blood.

sentences.zh: 聊城公茂少不闲礼教，长不务善道。

translations.literal: The Duke of Liaocheng Mao in youth was not versed in ritual instruction, in age did not pursue the good Way.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Liaocheng was never trained in ritual as a boy and never turned to virtue as a man.

sentences.zh: 先帝以为古之立诸侯也，皆命贤者，故姬姓有未必侯者，是以独不王茂。

translations.literal: The late emperor thought that in olden days when establishing the feudal lords they all ordered worthy men, therefore among the Ji surname there were those who were not necessarily marquises, and for this alone did not make Mao king.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor held that ancient enfeoffments went only to the worthy, so not every son of the house needed a kingdom—which is why Mao alone was denied a princely title.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后数以为言。

translations.literal: The grand empress dowager repeatedly spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: The grand empress dowager pleaded his case again and again.

sentences.zh: 如闻茂顷来少知悔昔之非，欲脩善将来。

translations.literal: As I have heard, Mao in recent times slightly knows to repent past faults and wishes to cultivate goodness for the future.
translations.idiomatic: I am told he has lately begun to regret his old errors and wants to mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 君子与其进，不保其往也。

translations.literal: The gentleman approves of his advance, and does not guarantee his past.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman encourages those who are improving and does not hold the past against them.

sentences.zh: 今封茂为聊城王，以慰太皇太后下流之念。

translations.literal: Now enfeoff Mao as king of Liaocheng, thereby to comfort the grand empress dowager's downstream thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore make him King of Liaocheng to answer the grand empress dowager's earnest plea on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 六年，改封曲阳王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year his fief was changed to Prince of Quyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 6 he was transferred to the princedom of Quyang.

sentences.zh: 正始三年，东平灵王薨，茂称嗌痛，不肯发哀，居处出入自若。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengshi the Prince Ling of Dongping died; Mao claimed pain in the throat, was unwilling to begin mourning, and dwelling and going out were as usual.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi 3, when Prince Ling of Dongping died, Mao claimed a sore throat, refused to enter mourning, and went about his daily routine unchanged.

sentences.zh: 有司奏除国土，诏削县一，户五百。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized to remove his territory; an edict stripped one county, 500 households.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers moved to strip his fief; the throne instead removed one county and five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 五年，徙封乐陵，诏以茂租奉少，诸子多，复所削户，又增户七百。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was moved to enfeoffment at Leling; an edict said because Mao's rent income was small and his sons many, restored the stripped households, and again increased households by 700.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi 5 he was moved to Leling. An edict noted his slender income and many sons, restored the lost households, and added seven hundred more.

sentences.zh: 嘉平、正元、景元中，累增邑，并前五千户。

translations.literal: In the Jiaping, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan periods his fief was repeatedly increased, totaling 5,000 households with the earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiaping, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan his appanage reached five thousand households in all.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝诸子

translations.literal: Sons of Emperor Wen of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Emperor Wen of Wei.

sentences.zh: 文皇帝九男：甄氏皇后生明帝，李贵人生赞哀王协，潘淑媛生北海悼王蕤，硃淑媛生东武阳怀王鉴，仇昭仪生东海定王霖，徐姬生元城哀王礼，苏姬生邯郸怀王邕，张姬生清河悼王贡，宋姬生广平哀王俨。

translations.literal: The Literary Emperor had nine sons: Empress Zhen bore Emperor Ming; Lady Li bore Prince Ai of Zan Xie; Lady Pan bore Prince Dao of Beihai Rui; Lady Zhu bore Prince Huai of Dongwuyang Jian; Lady Qiu bore Prince Ding of Donghai Lin; Lady Xu bore Prince Ai of Yuancheng Li; Lady Su bore Prince Huai of Handan Yong; Lady Zhang bore Prince Dao of Qinghe Gong; Lady Song bore Prince Ai of Guangping Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen had nine sons. Empress Zhen bore Emperor Ming; Lady Li bore Cao Xie, Prince Ai of Zan; Lady Pan bore Cao Rui of Beihai; Lady Zhu bore Cao Jian, Prince Huai of Dongwuyang; Lady Qiu bore Cao Lin, Prince Ding of Donghai; Lady Xu bore Cao Li, Prince Ai of Yuancheng; Lady Su bore Cao Yong, Prince Huai of Handan; Lady Zhang bore Cao Gong, Prince Dao of Qinghe; and Lady Song bore Cao Yan, Prince Ai of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 赞哀王曹协

translations.literal: Prince Ai of Zan, Cao Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xie, posthumously Prince Ai of Zan.

sentences.zh: 赞哀王协，早薨。

translations.literal: Prince Ai of Zan Xie died young.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xie died in childhood.

sentences.zh: 太和五年追封谥曰经殇公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe posthumous enfeoffment and posthumous title were conferred, titled Duke Jingshang.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 5 he was posthumously enfeoffed and given the title Duke Jingshang.

sentences.zh: 青龙二年，更追改号谥。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qinglong the title and posthumous name were again changed.
translations.idiomatic: In Qinglong 2 his posthumous rank and name were changed again.

sentences.zh: 三年，子殇王寻嗣。

translations.literal: In the third year the son Prince Shang Xun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In Qinglong 3 his son Cao Xun, posthumously Prince Shang, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 景初三年，增户五百，并前三千户。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingchu 500 households were added, totaling 3,000 households with the prior.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingchu 3 five hundred households were added, bringing the fief to three thousand.

sentences.zh: 正始九年薨。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengshi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhengshi 9.

sentences.zh: 无子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He had no heir.

sentences.zh: 国除。

translations.literal: The state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 北海悼王曹蕤

translations.literal: Prince Dao of Beihai, Cao Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Rui, posthumously Prince Dao of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 北海悼王蕤，黄初七年，明帝即位，立为阳平县王。

translations.literal: Prince Dao of Beihai Rui, in the seventh year of Huangchu, when Emperor Ming ascended, was established Prince of Yangping county.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 7, when Emperor Ming took the throne, Cao Rui was made Prince of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 太和六年，改封北海。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe his fief was changed to Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 6 he was transferred to Beihai.

sentences.zh: 青龙元年薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qinglong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qinglong 1.

sentences.zh: 二年，以琅邪王子赞奉蕤后，封昌乡公。

translations.literal: In the second year Zan, son of the Prince of Langye, was appointed to continue Rui's line, enfeoffed duke of Chang village.
translations.idiomatic: In Qinglong 2 Cao Zan, a son of the Prince of Langye, was named heir to Rui and made Duke of Chang district.

sentences.zh: 景初二年，立为饶安王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingchu he was established Prince of Rao'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingchu 2 he was raised to Prince of Rao'an.

sentences.zh: 正始七年，徙封文安。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhengshi he was moved to a fief at Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengshi 7 his seat moved to Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 正元、景元中，累增邑，并前三千五百户。

translations.literal: In the Zhengyuan and Jingyuan periods his fief was repeatedly increased, totaling 3,500 households with the earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengyuan and Jingyuan his appanage grew to 3,500 households in all.

sentences.zh: 东武阳怀王曹鉴

translations.literal: Prince Huai of Dongwuyang, Cao Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jian, posthumously Prince Huai of Dongwuyang.

sentences.zh: 东武阳怀王鉴，黄初六年立。

translations.literal: Prince Huai of Dongwuyang Jian, in the sixth year of Huangchu was established.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jian was enfeoffed in Huangchu 6.

sentences.zh: 其年薨。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the same year.

sentences.zh: 青龙三年赐谥。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qinglong posthumous title was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In Qinglong 3 he received a posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 无子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son.

sentences.zh: 国除。

translations.literal: The state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The line ended and the fief lapsed.

sentences.zh: 东海定王曹霖

translations.literal: Prince Ding of Donghai, Cao Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Lin, posthumously Prince Ding of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 东海定王霖，黄初三年立为河东王。

translations.literal: Prince Ding of Donghai Lin, in the third year of Huangchu was established Prince of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 3 Cao Lin was first made Prince of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 六年，改封馆陶县。

translations.literal: In the sixth year his fief was changed to Guantao county.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 6 his seat was moved to Guantao county.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，以先帝遗意，爱宠霖异於诸国。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended, according to the late emperor's dying intent, he loved and favored Lin differently from the various states.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, honoring his father's last wishes, showered singular favor on Cao Lin.

sentences.zh: 而霖性粗暴，闺门之内，婢妾之间，多所残害。

translations.literal: Yet Lin by nature was rough and violent; within the inner chambers, among maids and concubines, there was much killing and injury.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lin was a brute who terrorized the women of his household and killed many of them.

sentences.zh: 太和六年，改封东海。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe his fief was changed to Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 6 he was made Prince of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 嘉平元年薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaping he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiaping 1.

sentences.zh: 子启嗣。

translations.literal: His son Qi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao Qi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 景初、正元、景元中，累增邑，并前六千二百户。

translations.literal: In the Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan periods his fief was repeatedly increased, totaling 6,200 households with the earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan his fief swelled to 6,200 households.

sentences.zh: 高贵乡公髦，霖之子也，入继大宗。

translations.literal: Duke of Gaogui Township Mao was Lin's son; he entered to continue the great line.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Mao, Duke of Gaogui Township, was Lin's son and was brought in to continue the main imperial line.

sentences.zh: 元城哀王曹礼

translations.literal: Prince Ai of Yuancheng, Cao Li.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Li, posthumously Prince Ai of Yuancheng.

sentences.zh: 邯郸怀王曹邕

translations.literal: Prince Huai of Handan, Cao Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yong, posthumously Prince Huai of Handan.

sentences.zh: 邯郸怀王邕，黄初二年封淮南公，以九江郡为国。

translations.literal: Prince Huai of Handan Yong, in the second year of Huangchu was enfeoffed duke of Huainan, with Jiujiang commandery as the state.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 2 Cao Yong was made Duke of Huainan with Jiujiang as his appanage.

sentences.zh: 三年，进为淮南王。

translations.literal: In the third year he was advanced to Prince of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 3 he was promoted to Prince of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 四年，改封陈。

translations.literal: In the fourth year his fief was changed to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 4 he was transferred to Chen.

sentences.zh: 六年，改封邯郸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year his fief was changed to Handan.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu 6 he was moved to Handan.

sentences.zh: 太和三年薨。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taihe 3.

sentences.zh: 五年，以任城王楷子温嗣邕后。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Wen, son of the Prince of Rencheng Kai, was appointed to succeed Yong's line.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 5 Cao Wen, son of Prince Kai of Rencheng, was designated heir to Yong.

sentences.zh: 六年，改封鲁阳。

translations.literal: In the sixth year his fief was changed to Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 6 his seat was moved to Luyang.

sentences.zh: 景初、正元、景元中，累增邑，并前四千四百户。

translations.literal: In the Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan periods his fief was repeatedly increased, totaling 4,400 households with the earlier grants.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingchu, Zhengyuan, and Jingyuan his appanage grew to 4,400 households in all.

sentences.zh: 清河悼王曹贡

translations.literal: Prince Dao of Qinghe, Cao Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Gong, posthumously Prince Dao of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 清河悼王贡，黄初三年封。

translations.literal: Prince Dao of Qinghe Gong, in the third year of Huangchu was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Gong received his first enfeoffment in Huangchu 3.

sentences.zh: 四年薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Huangchu 4.

sentences.zh: 无子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir.

sentences.zh: 国除。

translations.literal: The state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 广平哀王曹俨

translations.literal: Prince Ai of Guangping, Cao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yan, posthumously Prince Ai of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 广平哀王俨，黄初三年封。

translations.literal: Prince Ai of Guangping Yan, in the third year of Huangchu was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yan was first enfeoffed in Huangchu 3.

sentences.zh: 四年薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year, in Huangchu 4.

sentences.zh: 无子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 国除。

translations.literal: The state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The line ended and the principality was struck from the rolls.

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: the historian's closing appraisal.

sentences.zh: 评曰：魏氏王公，既徒有国土之名，而无社稷之实，又禁防壅隔，同於囹圄；

translations.literal: The appraisal says: The princes and dukes of Wei had only the name of possessing territory, yet lacked the substance of altars of soil and grain; moreover prohibitions and defenses piled up and blocked them, the same as a prison.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Wei's princes bore territorial titles but held no real power over their domains; hedged by restrictions, they lived like men under lock and key.

sentences.zh: 位号靡定，大小岁易；

translations.literal: Ranks and titles were unsettled; great and small changed year by year.
translations.idiomatic: Titles shifted constantly, great and small alike reshuffled every year.

sentences.zh: 骨肉之恩乖，常棣之义废。

translations.literal: The grace of bone and flesh was violated; the righteousness of the "Changdi" ode was cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Kinship was strained and the brotherly duty praised in the Odes was forgotten.

sentences.zh: 为法之弊，一至于此乎！

translations.literal: The harm of the laws—did it reach this point!
translations.idiomatic: So far had the policy of control twisted the bonds of family!

sentences.zh: 〈《袁子》曰：魏兴，承大乱之后，民人损减，不可则以古始。

translations.literal: 〈The Yuanzi says: When Wei arose, it inherited the aftermath of great chaos; the people were diminished and could not be patterned on antiquity at the start.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Yuanzi observes: Wei rose after wholesale devastation; the population was too depleted to revive the full classical order at once.

sentences.zh: 於是封建侯王，皆使寄地，空名而无其实。

translations.literal: Thereupon in establishing feudal lords and kings they all made them lodge their lands elsewhere—empty names without reality.
translations.idiomatic: So the kings were given nominal fiefs far from any real domain they could govern.

sentences.zh: 王国使有老兵百餘人，以卫其国。

translations.literal: The princedom was given a little over a hundred old soldiers to guard the state.
translations.idiomatic: Each kingdom was allotted barely a hundred veteran guards.

sentences.zh: 虽有王侯之号，而乃侪为匹夫。

translations.literal: Although they had the titles of kings and marquises, they were classed the same as common men.
translations.idiomatic: They kept princely rank but were treated like commoners.

sentences.zh: 县隔千里之外，无朝聘之仪，邻国无会同之制。

translations.literal: Separated by counties a thousand li away, there was no ceremony of court visits; neighboring states had no system of joint meetings.
translations.idiomatic: Marooned a thousand li from court, they had no audience rites and no way to confer with fellow princes.

sentences.zh: 诸侯游猎不得过三十里，又为设防辅监国之官以伺察之。

translations.literal: The feudal lords in roaming and hunting could not pass thirty li, and moreover for them were established defender-tutor and overseer-of-state officials to spy and inspect them.
translations.idiomatic: They were forbidden to hunt more than thirty li from home, while minders and "state overseers" watched every move.

sentences.zh: 王侯皆思为布衣而不能得。

translations.literal: The kings and marquises all longed to be common cloth yet could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Many would gladly have traded their titles for a commoner's freedom and could not.

sentences.zh: 既违宗国籓屏之义，又亏亲戚骨肉之恩。

translations.literal: This both violated the meaning of the imperial clan as screen and shield, and injured the grace of bone-and-flesh kin.
translations.idiomatic: The policy betrayed both the purpose of enfeoffing kin as bulwarks and the claims of blood.

sentences.zh: 《魏氏春秋》载宗室曹冏上书曰：

translations.literal: The Wei shi chunqiu records a memorial from the clansman Cao Jiong:
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Annals preserve this memorial from the imperial clansman Cao Jiong:

sentences.zh: 臣闻古之王者，必建同姓以明亲亲，必树异姓以明贤贤。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the kings of antiquity surely established same-surname kin to clarify dear kin, surely planted different-surname houses to clarify worthy worthies.
translations.idiomatic: I have read that ancient kings enfeoffed kinsmen to honor family ties and raised unrelated houses to honor merit.

sentences.zh: 故传曰‘庸勋亲亲，昵近尊贤’；

translations.literal: Therefore the commentary says, "Reward merit, draw kin close, favor the near, honor the worthy";
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo tradition says: "Reward service, cherish kin, draw the near, honor the worthy";

sentences.zh: 书曰‘克明俊德，以亲九族’；

translations.literal: the Documents say, "Able to illumine splendid virtue, thereby to draw close the nine branches of the clan";
translations.idiomatic: the Documents say: "Cultivate bright virtue until the nine branches of the clan cleave to you";

sentences.zh: 诗云‘怀德维宁，宗子维城’。

translations.literal: the Odes say, "Cherish virtue and there is repose; the sons of the clan are the walls of the city."
translations.idiomatic: and the Odes sing: "Virtue brings peace; the royal nephews are the city walls."

sentences.zh: 由是观之，非贤无与兴功，非亲无与辅治。

translations.literal: From this viewing it, without worthies there is none to raise achievement; without kin there is none to assist governance.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows: without worthy men no great work is done; without kin no stable rule is kept.

sentences.zh: 夫亲亲之道，专用则其渐也微弱；

translations.literal: As for the way of drawing kin close, if used exclusively then its gradual effect is feeble;
translations.idiomatic: Rely on kin alone and their strength slowly ebbs;

sentences.zh: 贤贤之道，偏任则其弊也劫夺。

translations.literal: as for the way of honoring worthies, if one-sidedly employed then its harm is robbery and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: lean only on outsiders and you invite usurpation.

sentences.zh: 先圣知其然也，故博求亲疏而并用之；

translations.literal: The former sages knew it was thus; therefore they broadly sought near and distant and used both together;
translations.idiomatic: The sages knew this and balanced near and far, kin and stranger alike;

sentences.zh: 近则有宗盟籓卫之固，远则有仁贤辅弼之助，盛则有与共其治，衰则有与守其土，安则有与享其福，危则有与同其祸。

translations.literal: near then there was the firmness of clan covenants and screen-and-shield guard, far then there was the help of benevolent worthies as assistants; in flourishing there was sharing in governing together, in decline there was sharing in guarding the soil, in peace there was sharing in enjoying the blessing, in peril there was sharing in the same disaster.
