translations.idiomatic: so that at hand the house had the pledge of kin as rampart, and afar the aid of good ministers; in strength all shared the task of rule, in weakness all held the land, in peace all shared the blessing, in danger all shared the ruin.

sentences.zh: 夫然，故能有其国家，保其社稷，历纪长久，本枝百世也。

translations.literal: Being thus, therefore they were able to possess their states, preserve their altars of soil and grain, pass many reigns in long duration, root and branches for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: That is how dynasties kept their altars for ages, trunk and branches flourishing for centuries.

sentences.zh: 今魏尊尊之法虽明，亲亲之道未备。

translations.literal: Now Wei's law for honoring superiors is clear, yet the way of drawing kin close is not complete.
translations.idiomatic: Wei honors rank above kinship, but the way of cherishing blood has not been fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 诗不云乎，‘鹡鸰在原，兄弟急难’。

translations.literal: Does not the Odes say, "The wagtails are on the plain; brothers rush to one another's distress in calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Has not the Odes said, "The wagtails on the heath—brothers rush to help in extremity"?

sentences.zh: 以斯言之，明兄弟相救於丧乱之际，同心於忧祸之间，虽有阋墙之忿，不忘御侮之事。

translations.literal: Speaking from this, it clarifies that brothers rescue one another in the midst of ruin and chaos, are of one heart in the midst of worry and disaster; although there is resentment of quarreling within the wall, they do not forget the business of warding off insult from without.
translations.idiomatic: It means that brothers aid each other in collapse, stand together in peril, and even when they quarrel behind their own walls still close ranks against outsiders.

sentences.zh: 何则？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 忧患同也。

translations.literal: Worry and disaster are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Because they share the same peril.

sentences.zh: 今则不然，或任而不重，或释而不任，一旦疆埸称警，关门反拒，股肱不扶，胸心无卫。

translations.literal: Now it is not so: some are employed yet not heavily trusted, some are set aside yet not employed; once the borderlands cry alarm and the passes shut them out, the thigh and arm will not support them and the breast and belly have no guard.
translations.idiomatic: Today it is otherwise: kin are given office without real power, or shelved without use; when the frontier flares and the passes shut them away from court, they have no loyal arms to lean on and no shield for the heart of the state.

sentences.zh: 臣窃惟此，寝不安席，思献丹诚，贡策硃阙。

translations.literal: Your subject privately ponders this, cannot sleep peacefully on the mat, and wishes to offer cinnabar sincerity and present strategies at the vermilion gate.
translations.idiomatic: I lie awake thinking of it and wish to lay my loyal counsel before the crimson threshold.

sentences.zh: 谨撰合所闻，叙论成败。

translations.literal: Respectfully I have compiled what I have heard and set forth success and failure.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore set down what I know of rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 论曰：昔夏、殷、周历世数十，而秦二世而亡。

translations.literal: The discussion says: In olden days Xia, Yin, and Zhou passed through dozens of generations, yet Qin perished in two generations.
translations.idiomatic: Consider: Xia, Shang, and Zhou endured many reigns; Qin fell in two.

sentences.zh: 何则？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 三代之君，与天下共其民，故天下同其忧。

translations.literal: The lords of the Three Dynasties shared their people with all under Heaven, therefore all under Heaven shared their worries.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings shared power with the realm, and the realm shared their burdens.

sentences.zh: 秦王独制其民，故倾危而莫救。

translations.literal: The King of Qin alone controlled his people, therefore when it tilted to peril there was none to save.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor monopolized the people, so when crisis came no one came to his aid.

sentences.zh: 夫与民共其乐者，人必忧其忧；

translations.literal: He who shares joy with the people, people surely will worry his worries;
translations.idiomatic: Share the people's joys and they will shoulder your sorrows;

sentences.zh: 与民同其安者，人必拯其危。

translations.literal: he who shares peace with the people, people surely will rescue his peril.
translations.idiomatic: share their peace and they will rescue you from danger.

sentences.zh: 先王知独治之不能久也，故与人共治之；

translations.literal: The former kings knew that governing alone could not long endure; therefore they governed together with others;
translations.idiomatic: The sages knew sole rule could not last, so they ruled with others;

sentences.zh: 知独守之不能固也，故与人共守之。

translations.literal: knew that guarding alone could not be firm; therefore they guarded together with others.
translations.idiomatic: they knew lone defense could not hold, so they defended with others.

sentences.zh: 兼亲疏而两用，参同异而并建。

translations.literal: They combined near and distant and used both; mixed same and different and established both.
translations.idiomatic: They mixed kin and stranger, like and unlike, in one design.

sentences.zh: 是以轻重足以相镇，亲疏足以相卫，并兼路塞，逆节不生。

translations.literal: Therefore weight and lightness were sufficient mutually to stabilize, near and distant sufficient mutually to guard; roads to annexation were blocked and rebellious conduct did not arise.
translations.idiomatic: Weight balanced weight, near guarded far, paths to usurpation closed, and treason found no opening.

sentences.zh: 及其衰也，桓、文帅礼；

translations.literal: Coming to their decline, Huan and Wen led the rites;
translations.idiomatic: When they weakened, Duke Huan and Duke Wen upheld the ritual order;

sentences.zh: 苞茅不贡，齐师伐楚；

translations.literal: when the wrapped mao grass was not presented, Qi's army attacked Chu;
translations.idiomatic: when Chu failed to send the bundle of sacral grass, Qi marched against it;

sentences.zh: 宋不城周，晋戮其宰。

translations.literal: when Song did not wall Zhou, Jin executed its steward.
translations.idiomatic: when Song refused to wall the royal city, Jin executed its minister.

sentences.zh: 王纲弛而复张，诸侯傲而复肃。

translations.literal: The kingly net slackened yet was stretched again; the feudal lords were arrogant yet again became solemn.
translations.idiomatic: The royal net slackened, then tightened; arrogant lords were humbled again.

sentences.zh: 二霸之后，浸以陵迟。

translations.literal: After the two hegemons, gradually it declined.
translations.idiomatic: After those two hegemons the Zhou order slowly decayed.

sentences.zh: 吴、楚凭江，负固方城，虽心希九鼎，而畏迫宗姬，奸情散於胸怀，逆谋消於脣吻；

translations.literal: Wu and Chu relied on the Yangtze, bore their solidity on Fangcheng; although in heart they coveted the nine tripods, yet they feared and were pressed by the Ji-surname Zhou, treacherous feelings scattered in the breast and bosom, rebellious plans dissolved on the lips;
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Chu leaned on the Long River and Fangcheng's walls; though they coveted the nine tripods, the house of Zhou still cowed them—ambition died in the breast and plots died on the tongue.

sentences.zh: 斯岂非信重亲戚，任用贤能，枝叶硕茂，本根赖之与？

translations.literal: Was this not because kin were trusted heavily, worthies were employed, branches and leaves were lush and thick, and the root depended on them?
translations.idiomatic: Was it not because kin were trusted, worthies employed, the branches thick, and the root thereby secure?

sentences.zh: 自此之后，转相攻伐；

translations.literal: From this afterward they turned to attacking one another;
translations.idiomatic: Afterward they turned on one another;

sentences.zh: 吴并於越，晋分为三，鲁灭於楚，郑兼於韩。

translations.literal: Wu was annexed by Yue, Jin split into three, Lu was extinguished by Chu, Zheng was absorbed by Han.
translations.idiomatic: Wu fell to Yue, Jin split into three, Lu to Chu, Zheng to Han.

sentences.zh: 暨于战国，诸姬微矣，惟燕、卫独存，然皆弱小，西迫强秦，南畏齐、楚，忧惧灭亡，匪遑相恤。

translations.literal: Down to the Warring States period the various Ji were feeble; only Yan and Wei alone survived, yet both were small and weak, pressed by strong Qin in the west, fearing Qi and Chu in the south, worried and fearful of destruction, without leisure to pity one another.
translations.idiomatic: By the Warring States the Ji houses were frail; only Yan and Wei lingered, small states trapped between Qin in the west and Qi and Chu in the south, too busy saving themselves to help kin.

sentences.zh: 至於王赧，降为庶人，犹枝幹相持，得居虚位，海内无主，四十餘年。

translations.literal: Down to King Nan of Zhou, reduced to commoner, still branches and trunk supported one another, able to occupy empty position; within the seas there was no ruler for more than forty years.
translations.idiomatic: Even King Nan, demoted to commoner status, was propped up by kin for forty years of nominal kingship while the realm lacked a true sovereign.

sentences.zh: 秦据势胜之地，骋谲诈之术，征伐关东，蚕食九国，至於始皇，乃定天位。

translations.literal: Qin occupied terrain of victorious advantage, galloped deceitful stratagems, campaigned east of the passes, nibbled away the nine states; down to the First Emperor, then he settled the heavenly position.
translations.idiomatic: Qin held the high ground, wielded guile, marched east, devoured the nine regions, and the First Emperor seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 旷日若彼，用力若此，岂非深固根蒂不拔之道乎？

translations.literal: Days long like that, force used like this—was it not the way of deep firm root and base unuprootable?
translations.idiomatic: So long a climb, so heavy a cost—was that not the price of deep roots?

sentences.zh: 易曰；

translations.literal: The Changes says;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says:

sentences.zh: ‘其亡其亡，系于苞桑。

translations.literal: "Its perishing, its perishing—bound to the mulberry shoots."
translations.idiomatic: "Ruin, ruin—yet tied to the mulberry shoots at the root."

sentences.zh: ’周德其可谓当之矣。

translations.literal: Zhou's virtue can be called having matched this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's virtue matched that warning.

sentences.zh: 秦观周之弊，以为小弱见夺，於是废五等之爵，立郡县之官，弃礼乐之教，任苛刻之政；

translations.literal: Qin observed Zhou's harm, thought that being small and weak led to seizure; thereupon abolished the ranks of the five grades, established officials of commanderies and counties, cast aside ritual and music instruction, employed harsh and cutting government;
translations.idiomatic: Qin blamed Zhou's fall on weak princes, abolished the five ranks, set up commanderies and counties, scrapped ritual instruction, and ruled by terror;

sentences.zh: 子弟无尺寸之封，功臣无立锥之地，内无宗子以自毗辅，外无诸侯以为籓卫，仁心不加於亲戚，惠泽不流於枝叶；

translations.literal: sons and younger brothers had no enfeoffment of a foot or inch, merit ministers had no land the size of a awl-point; within there were no sons of the clan to support from the side, without there were no feudal lords to act as screen and shield; benevolent mind was not applied to kin, favoring grace did not flow to branches and leaves;
translations.idiomatic: no prince held an inch of soil, no minister a handspan of ground; no kinsman buttressed the throne within, no prince guarded the marches without; mercy never reached family, bounty never reached the boughs;

sentences.zh: 譬犹芟刈股肱，独任胸腹，浮舟江海，捐弃楫棹，观者为之寒心，而始皇晏然自以为关中之固，金城千里，子孙帝王万世之业也，岂不悖哉！

translations.literal: it was like mowing off thigh and arm, alone trusting breast and belly, floating a boat on river and sea yet casting away oar and scull—observers for it were chilled at heart, yet the First Emperor was calm and thought the barrier within the passes secure, metal walls a thousand li, the enterprise of emperors and kings for myriad generations of sons and grandsons—was it not contrary?
translations.idiomatic: as if cutting off one's own limbs yet trusting only the trunk, or putting to sea without oars—onlookers shuddered while the First Emperor slept easy behind his "metal city" and dreamed of an eternal line!

sentences.zh: 是时淳于越谏曰：‘臣闻殷、周之王，封子弟功臣千有餘

translations.literal: At that time Chunyu Yue remonstrated, saying, "Your subject has heard that the kings of Yin and Zhou enfeoffed sons and merit ministers to more than a thousand
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Yue then urged: "The kings of Yin and Zhou enfeoffed sons and merit ministers in more than a thousand

translations.literal: (The gloss supplies the word "city" or "cities.")
translations.idiomatic: the gloss supplies the word "cities,"

translations.literal: Period (marking the end of the quoted sentence).
translations.idiomatic: closing that clause of his memorial.

sentences.zh: 今陛下君有海内而子弟为匹夫，卒有田常六卿之臣，而无辅弼，何以相救？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty rules all within the seas yet sons and younger brothers are common men; if suddenly there appear subjects like Tian Chang or the six ministers of Jin, yet there are no assistants, how shall one rescue one another?
translations.idiomatic: Now you rule the realm while your brothers are mere commoners; should a Tian Chang or a six-minister cabal arise, what bulwark will save the throne?

sentences.zh: 事不师古而能长久者，非所闻也。

translations.literal: Matters that do not take antiquity as teacher yet can long endure—this is not what I have heard of.
translations.idiomatic: I have never heard of an enduring throne that refused to learn from the past."

sentences.zh: ’始皇听李斯偏说而绌其议，至於身死之日，无所寄付，委天下之重於凡夫之手，讬废立之命於奸臣之口，至令赵高之徒，诛鉏宗室。

translations.literal: The First Emperor listened to Li Si's one-sided doctrine and rejected his proposal; down to the day of his death there was nothing to entrust the charge to, he entrusted the weight of all under Heaven to the hands of a vulgar man, entrusted the mandate of deposing and establishing to the mouth of a treacherous minister, until followers like Zhao Gao slaughtered the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor took Li Si's narrow counsel and dismissed Chunyu Yue; at his death he had no one to whom he could turn, handed the realm to a mediocrity, and left the succession to a villain—so Zhao Gao could butcher the royal house.

sentences.zh: 胡亥少习刻薄之教，长遭凶父之业，不能改制易法，宠任兄弟，而乃师谭申、商，谘谋赵高；

translations.literal: Ershi in youth was habituated to cutting and carving instruction, in age encountered the enterprise of a cruel father, was unable to reform institutions and change laws, favor and trust brothers, but instead took as teachers Shen and Shang, took counsel with Zhao Gao;
translations.idiomatic: The Second Emperor grew up on harsh teaching and inherited a tyrant's legacy; instead of reforming the laws and trusting his brothers he studied the Legalists Shen and Shang and listened to Zhao Gao;

sentences.zh: 自幽深宫，委政谗贼，身残望夷，求为黔首，岂可得哉？

translations.literal: from himself hiding deep in the palace, he entrusted government to slanderous villains, mutilated himself at Wangyi, sought to be a black-headed commoner—could it be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: he hid in the inner palace while traitors ruled, was driven to suicide at the Wangyi Pavilion, and begged to end his days as a commoner—an end he could not buy?

sentences.zh: 遂乃郡国离心，众庶溃叛，胜、广倡之於前，刘、项弊之於后。

translations.literal: Thereupon commanderies and states turned their hearts away, the multitude scattered in rebellion, Chen Sheng and Wu Guang raised them in front, Liu and Xiang wore them down behind.
translations.idiomatic: The provinces turned away, the people rose, Chen Sheng and Wu Guang struck first, Liu Bang and Xiang Yu finished the work.

sentences.zh: 向使始皇纳淳于之策，抑李斯之论，割裂州国，分王子弟，封三代之后，报功臣之劳，士有常君，民有定主，枝叶相扶，首尾为用，虽使子孙有失道之行，时人无汤、武之贤，奸谋未发，而身已屠戮，何区区之陈、项而复得措其手足哉？

translations.literal: Supposing the First Emperor had accepted Chunyu's plan, restrained Li Si's doctrine, carved apart provinces and states, divided and enfeoffed sons and younger brothers, enfeoffed the descendants of the Three Dynasties, repaid the toil of merit ministers—officers had constant lords, the people had fixed masters, branches and leaves supported one another, head and tail served as useful: although descendants had conduct of losing the Way, men of the time lacked the worthiness of Tang and Wu, treacherous plots had not yet issued yet the body was already slaughtered—how could petty Chen and Xiang again get to place their hands and feet?
translations.idiomatic: Had the First Emperor heeded Chunyu Yue, split the realm among princes, enfeoffed the heirs of the three ancient dynasties, and rewarded his ministers—had every officer known his lord and every peasant his master, with kin like limbs to the trunk—even vicious heirs could not have brought down the house before usurpers appeared; how then could two bandits have toppled Qin?

sentences.zh: 故汉祖奋三尺之剑，驱乌集之众，五年之中，遂成帝业。

translations.literal: Therefore the Han founder flourished a three-foot sword, drove a flock of crows gathered multitude, and within five years then completed the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: So the Han founder waved a common sword, led a rabble in arms, and within five years sat as emperor.

sentences.zh: 自开辟以来，其兴立功勋，未有若汉祖之易也。

translations.literal: From the opening of the age, none who raised merit and established deeds has been as easy as the Han founder.
translations.idiomatic: Since time began no one won an empire as easily as Liu Bang.

sentences.zh: 夫伐深根者难为功，摧枯朽者易为力，理势然也。

translations.literal: Cutting deep roots is hard to accomplish merit; smashing withered rot is easy to accomplish force—pattern and circumstance are thus.
translations.idiomatic: Deep roots resist the axe; dry rot yields at a touch—that is the way of things.

sentences.zh: 汉监秦之失，封殖子弟，及诸吕擅权，图危刘氏，而天下所以不倾动，百姓所以不易心者，徒以诸侯强大，盘石胶固，东牟、硃虚受命於内，齐、代、吴、楚作卫於外故也。

translations.literal: Han took warning from Qin's failure, enfeoffed and planted sons and younger brothers; when the various Lü monopolized power and plotted danger to the Liu house, the reason all under Heaven did not tilt and shift, the reason the hundred surnames did not change heart, was solely because the feudal lords were strong and great, solid as glued stone, Dongmou and Zhuxu received orders within, Qi, Dai, Wu, and Chu acted as guard without.
translations.idiomatic: Han learned from Qin and enfeoffed kin; when the Lü clan seized power the realm did not crumble because the princes were strong as set stone—Liu Zhang and Liu Xingju acted inside the capital while Qi, Dai, Wu, and Chu guarded the frontiers.

sentences.zh: 向使高祖踵亡秦之法，忽先王之制，则天下已传，非刘氏有也。

translations.literal: Supposing Gaozu had followed the extinguished Qin's laws, neglected the former kings' institutions, then all under Heaven would have shifted transmission and would not have been possessed by the Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Had Gaozu copied Qin's system and scorned the ancients, the empire would have passed from the Liu before the Lü ever stirred.

sentences.zh: 然高祖封建，地过古制，大者跨州兼郡，小者连城数十，上下无别，权侔京室，故有吴、楚七国之患。

translations.literal: Yet Gaozu's enfeoffments crossed the ancient measure in land: the great spanned provinces and combined commanderies, the small linked several tens of cities; high and low had no distinction, power matched the capital precincts; therefore there was the disaster of Wu and Chu and the seven states.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Han fiefs were oversized: the greatest swallowed whole provinces, the smallest chained dozens of cities, rivaling the capital—hence the revolt of the seven kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 贾谊曰：‘诸侯强盛，长乱起奸。

translations.literal: Jia Yi said, "The feudal lords are strong and flourishing, long disorder and rising treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi warned: "Powerful vassals breed long chaos and treason.

sentences.zh: 夫欲天下之治安，莫若众建诸侯而少其力，令海内之势，若身之使臂，臂之使指，则下无背叛之心，上无诛伐之事。

translations.literal: If one desires peace and order for all under Heaven, nothing compares to establishing many feudal lords yet diminishing their strength, ordering the power within the seas like the body commanding the arm, the arm commanding the finger—then below there is no heart of rebellion, above there is no business of execution and attack."
translations.idiomatic: To keep the realm at peace, split their strength among many fiefs so that power runs from the throne to the arm to the finger—then subjects will not rebel and the sovereign need not punish."

sentences.zh: ’文帝不从。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen ignored him.

sentences.zh: 至於孝景，猥用晁错之计，削黜诸侯，亲者怨恨，疏者震恐，吴、楚倡谋，五国从风。

translations.literal: Coming to Emperor Xiaojing, rashly he used Chao Cuo's plan, stripped and dismissed the feudal lords; the close resented, the distant trembled in fear; Wu and Chu raised the plot, five states followed the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing rashly adopted Chao Cuo's policy of stripping the fiefs; close kin grew bitter, distant kin afraid; Wu and Chu rebelled and five states followed.

sentences.zh: 兆发高帝，衅锺文、景，由宽之过制，急之不渐故也。

translations.literal: The omen issued from Gaodi, the blame fell on Wen and Jing—because of looseness that crossed measure, urgency that lacked gradualness.
translations.idiomatic: The seeds lay with Gaozu, the reckoning with Wen and Jing—first they let the princes grow too strong, then they cut them too fast.

sentences.zh: 所谓末大必折，尾大难掉。

translations.literal: What is called the end being large must break, the tail being large is hard to wag.
translations.idiomatic: As the adage runs: limbs too heavy will snap; a tail too big cannot wag.

sentences.zh: 尾同於体，犹或不从，况乎非体之尾，其可掉哉？

translations.literal: The tail being the same as the body, still sometimes does not obey—how much more when the tail is not of the body—can it be wagged?
translations.idiomatic: Even a tail of one's own body may disobey—how much less a tail that is not of the body?

sentences.zh: 武帝从主父之策，下推恩之令，自是之后，齐分为七，赵分为六，淮南三割，梁、代五分，遂以陵迟，子孙微弱，衣食租税，不预政事，或以酎金免削，或以无后国除。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu followed Zhufu's strategy, issued the decree of pushing grace downward; from this afterward Qi split into seven, Zhao split into six, Huainan was thrice carved, Liang and Dai fivefold split, thereby gradually declined, sons and grandsons feeble and small, living on rent and tax, not participating in government affairs, some by ritual gold offering were stripped and cut, some by having no successor the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu applied Zhufu Yan's "grace extension" edict: Qi fractured into seven, Zhao into six, Huainan was carved thrice, Liang and Dai split repeatedly, until the princes dwindled to rent-collectors barred from politics—many lost fiefs for the "sacrificial gold" fault or for lack of heirs.

sentences.zh: 至於成帝，王氏擅朝。

translations.literal: Coming to Emperor Cheng, the Wang clan monopolized the court.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Cheng the Wang clan ran the court.

sentences.zh: 刘向谏曰：‘臣闻公族者，国之枝叶；

translations.literal: Liu Xiang remonstrated, saying, "Your subject has heard that the ducal houses are the branches and leaves of the state;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang warned: "The imperial clan is the foliage of the throne;

sentences.zh: 枝叶落则本根无所庇廕。

translations.literal: when branches and leaves fall then root and base have nothing to shelter and shade.
translations.idiomatic: strip the leaves and the root stands naked to wind and sun."

sentences.zh: 方今同姓疏远，母党专政，排摈宗室，孤弱公族，非所以保守社稷，安固国嗣也。

translations.literal: Now same-surname kin are distant, the maternal faction monopolizes government, pushes aside the imperial clan, isolates and weakens the ducal houses—this is not the means to preserve the altars of soil and grain and settle and secure the succession of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Today imperial kinsmen are kept at arm's length while in-laws run the government, the house of Liu is elbowed aside, and the princes are left powerless—that is no way to guard the dynasty or secure the heir.

sentences.zh: ’其言深切，多所称引，成帝虽悲伤叹息而不能用。

translations.literal: His words were profound and cutting, and cited many authorities; Emperor Cheng although grieved and sighed could not employ them.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial was trenchant and packed with precedent, yet Emperor Cheng could only sigh and set it aside.

sentences.zh: 至於哀、平，异姓秉权，假周公之事，而为田常之乱，高拱而窃天位，一朝而臣四海。

translations.literal: Down to Ai and Ping, different surnames grasped power, borrowing the deeds of the Duke of Zhou yet working the disorder of Tian Chang, hands folded high while stealing the heavenly position, in one morning making all within the seas his subjects.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperors Ai and Ping outsiders held the reins, masked as the Duke of Zhou while acting like Tian Chang—Wang Mang folded his hands on the throne and in a single morning made the realm his vassal.

sentences.zh: 汉宗室王侯，解印释绂，贡奉社稷，犹惧不得为臣妾，或乃为之符命，颂莽恩德，岂不哀哉！

translations.literal: Han imperial-clansmen kings and marquises, unsealing seals and loosing ribbons, offering up the altars of soil and grain, still feared not obtaining the status of subject and handmaiden, some even forged talisman-mandates praising Mang's grace and virtue—was it not pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: Han princes surrendered their seals and yielded the altars, yet still feared they might not be spared even as slaves; some forged omens praising Wang Mang—what a spectacle of humiliation!

sentences.zh: 由斯言之，非宗子独忠孝於惠、文之间，而叛逆於哀、平之际也，徒权轻势弱，不能有定耳。

translations.literal: From this speaking, it was not that the sons of the clan alone were loyal and filial between Hui and Wen, yet rebellious in the crisis of Ai and Ping—solely their authority was light and power weak, unable to have stability.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu princes were not loyal by nature under Huidi and Wendi and treacherous by nature under Ai and Ping—they simply lacked the power to be anything else.

sentences.zh: 赖光武皇帝挺不世之姿，禽王莽於已成，绍汉嗣於既绝，斯岂非宗子之力也？

translations.literal: Relying on Emperor Guangwu's raising a posture not of the age, capturing Wang Mang when already accomplished, continuing Han's succession when already cut off—was this not the strength of the sons of the clan?
translations.idiomatic: When Guangwu seized Wang Mang and restored the Han, was that not the proof of what royal kin can do?

sentences.zh: 而曾不监秦之失策，袭周之旧制，踵王国之法，而徼倖无疆之期。

translations.literal: Yet he did not take warning from Qin's failed policy, inherited Zhou's old institutions, followed the law of kingly states, and hoped without boundary for long fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he did not learn from Qin's mistake, copied Zhou's old enfeoffment, revived great princedoms, and gambled on endless good luck.

sentences.zh: 至於桓、灵，阉竖执衡，朝无死难之臣，外无同忧之国，君孤立於上，臣弄权於下，本末不能相御，身首不能相使。

translations.literal: Down to Huan and Ling, eunuchs held the balance; within the court there were no ministers who died for difficulty; without there were no states sharing worry; the lord stood alone above, ministers toyed with power below; root and tip could not mutually control, body and head could not mutually command.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperors Huan and Ling the eunuchs held power: no minister died for the throne, no prince shared the peril; the emperor stood alone while ministers pulled the strings; head and limbs no longer answered to one another.

sentences.zh: 由是天下鼎沸，奸凶并争，宗庙焚为灰烬，宫室变为榛薮，居九州之地，而身无所安处，悲夫！

translations.literal: Thereupon all under Heaven boiled like a cauldron, treacherous villains together strove, the ancestral temple burned to ashes, palace halls turned to thickets; occupying the land of the nine provinces, yet the body had nowhere to rest—alas!
translations.idiomatic: The empire boiled into civil war, the ancestral shrines burned to ash, palaces went to weed, and the Son of Heaven had not a foot of ground to call his own—what ruin!

sentences.zh: 魏太祖武皇帝躬圣明之资，兼神武之略，耻王纲之废绝，愍汉室之倾覆，龙飞谯、沛，凤翔兗、豫，扫除凶逆，翦灭鲸鲵，迎帝西京，定都颍邑，德动天地，义感人神。

translations.literal: Wei's Grand Progenitor the Martial Emperor personally had sage-bright substance, combined with spirit-martial strategy, took shame in the kingly net's ruin and severance, pitied the Han house's overturning; dragon flew at Qiao and Pei, phoenix soared at Yan and Yu, swept away fierce rebels, cut down great whales, welcomed the emperor to western capital, settled the capital at Yingyi, virtue moved heaven and earth, righteousness stirred men and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao bore both wisdom and martial genius; he grieved for the fallen Han, rose in Qiao and Pei, swept the rebels, welcomed the emperor west, and moved the court to Xuchang—his virtue shook heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 汉氏奉天，禅位大魏。

translations.literal: The Han house received Heaven's mandate and yielded the throne to great Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Han then yielded the mandate to Wei.

sentences.zh: 大魏之兴，于今二十有四年矣，观五代之存亡而不用其长策，睹前车之倾覆而不改於辙迹；

translations.literal: Great Wei's rise, to now is already twenty-four years; observing the survival and perishing of five dynasties yet not using their long strategy, seeing the overturning of the cart ahead yet not changing the rut tracks;
translations.idiomatic: Wei has now stood twenty-four years, yet it watches five dynasties rise and fall without taking their long view, and sees the overturned cart ahead without steering clear of its ruts;

sentences.zh: 子弟王空虚之地，君有不使之民，宗室窜於闾阎，不闻邦国之政，权均匹夫，势齐凡庶；

translations.literal: sons and younger brothers are kings of empty lands, lords have people they may not employ, the imperial clan hides in lanes and alleys, do not hear the government of states and polities, authority equals the common man, power matches the vulgar crowd;
translations.idiomatic: princes hold hollow titles over people they cannot command, kinsmen skulk in back alleys and hear no state business, and their rank weighs no more than a commoner's;

sentences.zh: 内无深根不拔之固，外无盘石宗盟之助，非所以安社稷，为万世之业也。

translations.literal: within there is no firmness of deep roots unuprootable, without there is no help of glued-stone clan covenant—this is not the means to settle the altars of soil and grain and make enterprise for myriad generations.
translations.idiomatic: there is no deep taproot within, no princely bulwark without—hardly a design to secure the altars for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 且今之州牧、郡守，古之方伯、诸侯，皆跨有千里之土，兼军武之任，或比国数人，或兄弟并据；

translations.literal: Moreover today's provincial shepherds and commandery governors are the ancient regional lords and feudal marquises, all striding to possess soil of a thousand li, combining military office, some several men compared to a state, some brothers together occupying;
translations.idiomatic: Today's governors are the old regional lords: each holds a thousand li, commands troops, and some kinsmen share whole provinces between them;

sentences.zh: 而宗室子弟曾无一人间厕其间，与相维持，非所以强幹弱枝，备万一之虞也。

translations.literal: yet among imperial-clansmen sons and younger brothers there is not one person wedged in their midst to mutually uphold them—this is not the means to strengthen the trunk and weaken the branches, prepare for the contingency of one in ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: yet not a single imperial prince sits among them as counterweight—this is no way to thicken the trunk and thin the branches against a sudden storm.

sentences.zh: 今之用贤，或超为名都之主，或为偏师之帅，而宗室有文者必限小县之宰，有武者必置百人之上，使夫廉高之士，毕志於衡轭之内，才能之人，耻与非类为伍，非所以劝进贤能褒异宗室之礼也。

translations.literal: Now in employing worthies, some leap to become masters of famous capitals, some become commanders of detached armies, yet if the imperial clan has literary talent they must be limited to magistrate of a small county, if martial they must be placed above a hundred men, causing those of integrity and high conduct to exhaust their ambition within the yoke and crossbar, men of ability and talent to be ashamed to stand in ranks with the non-kindred—this is not the ritual of encouraging advancement of worthies and praising the exceptional among the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Outsiders leap to govern great cities or lead armies, while a learned prince is capped as county magistrate and a brave one as captain of a hundred—so the worthy among the blood royal choke in low office and shrink from serving beneath parvenus. That is no way to honor talent in the clan.

sentences.zh: 夫泉竭则流涸，根朽则叶枯；

translations.literal: When the spring is exhausted then the flow dries;
translations.idiomatic: When the spring fails the stream runs dry;

sentences.zh: 枝繁者廕根，条落者本孤。

translations.literal: when branches are luxuriant they shade the root, when twigs fall the base stands alone.
translations.idiomatic: lush branches shade the root, stripped branches leave the trunk bare.

sentences.zh: 故语曰‘百足之虫，至死不殭’，以扶之者众也。

translations.literal: Therefore the saying goes, "The centipede's insect, to death is not stiff"—because those who support it are many.
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says, "The hundred-foot worm dies stiff"—because many legs still prop it up.

sentences.zh: 此言虽小，可以譬大。

translations.literal: Though this saying is small, it can illustrate the large.
translations.idiomatic: A small image can frame a great truth.

sentences.zh: 且墉基不可仓卒而成，威名不可一朝而立，皆为之有渐，建之有素。

translations.literal: Moreover foundation walls cannot be completed in haste, awe-inspiring name cannot be established in one morning—all are done for it with gradualness, built for it with constancy.
translations.idiomatic: Foundations are not laid in a day, nor renown won in a morning; both demand steady, long work.

sentences.zh: 譬之种树，久则深固其本根，茂盛其枝叶，若造次徙於山林之中，植於宫阙之下，虽壅之以黑坟，暖之以春日，犹不救於枯槁，而何暇繁育哉？

translations.literal: Compare to planting trees: long then deeply firm its root base, luxuriant its branches and leaves; if hastily moved amid mountains and forests, planted beneath palace gates, although banked with black soil, warmed with spring sun, still it will not save from withering—how then have leisure to breed and multiply?
translations.idiomatic: Think of trees: years deepen the roots and thicken the crown; wrench a sapling from the hills and stick it under the palace eaves, heap black earth on it and warm it in spring sun—it will still wither, let alone bear seed?

sentences.zh: 夫树犹亲戚，土犹士民，建置不久，则轻下慢上，平居犹惧其离叛，危急将若之何？

translations.literal: Trees are like kin, soil is like officers and people; if establishment is not long, then below is light and above is scorned; in ordinary peace one still fears their separation and rebellion—in crisis what shall be done?
translations.idiomatic: The tree is kin, the soil the people; a shallow planting makes subjects scorn their lords even in quiet times—what then when danger strikes?

sentences.zh: 是以圣王安而不逸，以虑危也，存而设备，以惧亡也。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage king is secure yet not idle, thereby pondering peril; exists yet prepares equipment, thereby fearing perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the sage king rests secure but never idly, always mindful of peril; he lives at ease yet lays in safeguards against ruin.

sentences.zh: 故疾风卒至而无摧拔之忧，天下有变而无倾危之患矣。

translations.literal: Therefore swift wind suddenly arrives yet there is no worry of snapping and uprooting; all under Heaven has change yet there is no worry of overturning peril.
translations.idiomatic: Then sudden storms will not snap the tree, and turmoil in the realm will not topple the throne.

sentences.zh: 冏，中常侍兄叔兴之后，少帝族祖也。

translations.literal: Jiong was of the posterity of the elder brother Shuxing of a palace attendant, a distant paternal clansman of the young emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jiong was a descendant of Shuxing, elder brother of a ranking eunuch at court, and a remote kinsman of the boy emperor.

sentences.zh: 是时天子幼稚，冏冀以此论感悟曹爽，爽不能纳。〉

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was young and childish; Jiong hoped by this discourse to awaken and move Cao Shuang; Shuang could not accept it.〉
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign was still a child; Jiong meant this memorial to rouse Cao Shuang, but Shuang would not heed it.〉
